title.zh: 卷一百九十九 志第一百五十二 刑法一
title.raw: 卷一百九十九 志第一百五十二 刑法一 Volume 199 Treatises 152: Punishment and Law 1

sentences.zh: 夫天有五氣以育萬物，木德以生，金德以殺，亦甚盭矣，而始終之序，相成之道也。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has five qi to nurture the myriad things; the virtue of wood gives life, the virtue of metal brings killing—how harsh that is—yet the sequence from beginning to end is the way of mutual completion.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends forth five vital forces to nourish the myriad creatures: the virtue of wood fosters life, and the virtue of metal brings death—harsh as that may seem—yet the cycle from beginning to end is the very principle by which they complete one another.

sentences.zh: 先天有刑罰以糾其民，則必溫慈惠和以行之，蓋裁之以義，推之以仁，則震殺戮之威，非求民之死，所以求其生也。

translations.literal: When Heaven first has punishments to correct the people, it must carry them out with warmth, kindness, beneficence, and harmony. For if one trims with righteousness and extends with benevolence, then the awe of killing and slaughter is not to seek the people's death but to seek their life.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven first institutes punishments to correct the people, it must apply them with warmth, kindness, beneficence, and harmony. Trim with righteousness and extend with benevolence, and the dread of killing becomes not a quest for the people's death but a means to secure their life.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。」

translations.literal: The Book says: "The officer regulates the hundred surnames within punishments, to teach reverent virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "The officer sets the common people within the bounds of punishment, to teach them reverent virtue."

sentences.zh: 言刑以弼教，使之畏威遠罪，導以之善爾。

translations.literal: It means that punishments assist instruction, making them fear awe and keep away from crime, and guiding them toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: That is to say, punishment assists instruction: it makes people fear authority and shun crime, and guides them toward what is good.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之治，固不能廢刑也；

translations.literal: Under the governance of Tang and Yu, punishments certainly could not be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Even under the rule of Tang and Yu, punishments could not be dispensed with;

sentences.zh: 惟禮以防之，有弗及，則刑以輔之而已。

translations.literal: only rites were used to guard against wrongdoing, and where that fell short, punishments merely supplemented them.
translations.idiomatic: rites alone were relied on to prevent wrongdoing, and only where rites fell short did punishment serve as a supplement.

sentences.zh: 王道陵遲，禮制隳廢，始專任法以罔其民，於是作為 刑書，欲民無犯，而亂獄滋豐，由其本末無序，不足相成故也。

translations.literal: When the kingly way declined and ritual institutions were ruined and abandoned, rulers began to rely solely on law to ensnare the people. Thereupon they composed penal codes, wishing that the people would not offend, yet disorder in the prisons grew ever more abundant—because root and branch were out of order and insufficient to complete one another.
translations.idiomatic: As the kingly way declined and ritual institutions fell into ruin, rulers came to rely on law alone to trap the people. They drafted penal codes in the hope that no one would offend, yet chaos in the courts only multiplied—because they had lost the proper order of root and branch and could no longer support one another.

sentences.zh: 宋興，承五季之亂，太祖、太宗頗用重典，以繩姦慝，歲時躬自折獄慮囚，務底明慎，而以忠厚為本。

translations.literal: When the Song arose, inheriting the chaos of the Five Dynasties, Taizu and Taizong rather often employed severe statutes to restrain treachery and wickedness; each year they personally heard cases and reviewed prisoners, striving for clarity and caution, with loyalty and generosity as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty rose, inheriting the turmoil of the Five Dynasties, Taizu and Taizong often applied severe laws to restrain treachery and wickedness. Year after year they personally presided over trials and reviewed prisoners, aiming at clarity and caution while taking loyalty and generosity as their foundation.

sentences.zh: 海內悉平，文教寖盛，士初試官，皆習律令。

translations.literal: When all within the seas was pacified, literary culture gradually flourished, and when scholars first entered office they all studied statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was fully pacified, literary culture gradually flourished, and scholars newly entering office all studied statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 其君一以寬仁為治，故立法之制嚴，而用法之情恕。

translations.literal: Their rulers uniformly took lenience and benevolence as the basis of governance; therefore the system of legislation was strict, yet the spirit in applying the law was forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Their rulers consistently governed with lenience and benevolence, so that although the letter of the law was strict, the spirit in which it was applied was forgiving.

sentences.zh: 獄有小疑，覆奏輒得減宥。

translations.literal: If a case held the slightest doubt, upon memorial review reduction or pardon was usually granted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a case raised the slightest doubt, a memorial for review usually brought reduction of sentence or pardon.

sentences.zh: 觀夫重熙累洽之際，天下之民咸樂其生，重於犯法，而致治之盛幾乎三代之懿。

translations.literal: Observing the era of repeated radiance and accumulated harmony, the people throughout the realm all delighted in their lives and valued avoiding offense, and the splendor of good governance nearly matched the excellence of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In that era of repeated radiance and accumulated harmony, the people throughout the realm delighted in life and shrank from breaking the law, and the height of good government nearly matched the excellence of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 元豐以來，刑書益繁，已而憸邪並進，刑政紊矣。

translations.literal: From the Yuanfeng era onward, penal writings grew ever more numerous; soon crafty and wicked men advanced together, and penal administration fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuanfeng era onward, penal codes grew ever more numerous; before long crafty and wicked men rose together, and criminal administration fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 國既南遷，威柄下逮，州郡之吏亦頗專行，而刑之寬猛繫乎其人。

translations.literal: After the state moved south, authority descended to lower levels, and prefectural and district officials also rather often acted on their own, so that whether punishments were lenient or severe depended on the person.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, authority devolved to lower levels, and prefectural and district officials often acted on their own, so whether punishment was lenient or severe depended on who held office.

sentences.zh: 然累世猶知以愛民為心，雖其失慈弱，而祖宗之遺意蓋未泯焉。

translations.literal: Yet for successive generations they still knew to take love of the people as their heart; although they fell short in being overly tender and weak, the legacy intent of the ancestral founders had not yet perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for generations they still took love of the people to heart; though they sometimes erred on the side of excessive lenience, the founding ancestors' intent had not yet been extinguished.

sentences.zh: 今摭其實，作《刑法志》。

translations.literal: Now gathering the facts, I compose the "Treatise on Punishment and Law."
translations.idiomatic: Here I gather the facts and compose the Treatise on Punishment and Law.

sentences.zh: 宋法制因唐律、令、格、式，而隨時損益，則有編敕，一司、一路、一州、一縣又別有敕。

translations.literal: Song legal institutions followed the Tang categories of lü, ling, ge, and shi, but with additions and reductions according to the times there were compiled edicts (bianchi), and each bureau, circuit, prefecture, and county also had separate edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Song law followed the Tang framework of statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms, but as circumstances changed there came compiled edicts, and each bureau, circuit, prefecture, and county had edicts of its own besides.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，詔判大理寺竇儀等上《編敕》四卷，凡一百有六條，詔與新定《刑統》三十卷並頒天下，參酌輕重為詳，世稱平允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, an edict ordered Dou Yi, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and others to present the Compiled Edicts in four juan, altogether one hundred and six articles; an edict ordered them promulgated throughout the realm together with the newly revised Penal Code in thirty juan. Weighing severity and leniency in detail, the age called them fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong reign, the court ordered Dou Yi of the Court of Judicial Review and others to submit the Compiled Edicts in four scrolls, 106 articles in all, and promulgated them empire-wide together with the newly revised thirty-scroll Penal Code. Because they carefully balanced severity and leniency, contemporaries praised them as fair.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，增敕至十五卷，淳化中倍之。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo period, the edicts were increased to fifteen juan; in the Chunhua period they were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo the edicts grew to fifteen scrolls; in the Chunhua era they doubled again.

sentences.zh: 咸平中增至萬八千五百五十有五條，詔給事中柴成務等芟其繁亂，定可為敕者二百八十有六條，準律分十二門，總十一卷。

translations.literal: In Xianping they increased to eighteen thousand five hundred and fifty-five articles. An edict ordered the Supervising Secretary Chai Chengwu and others to cut away what was redundant and disorderly, fixing two hundred and eighty-six articles that could serve as edicts, divided into twelve sections according to the statutes, eleven juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xianping era they had swollen to 18,555 articles. The court ordered Supervising Secretary Chai Chengwu and others to prune the redundancies and fix 286 articles as proper edicts, arranged in twelve sections after the statutes, eleven scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 又為《儀制令》一卷。

translations.literal: They also made the Ceremonial Regulations Ordinance in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: They also compiled the Ceremonial Regulations Ordinance in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 當時便其簡易。

translations.literal: At the time people found its simplicity convenient.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time welcomed its simplicity.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu period.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era.

sentences.zh: 又增三十卷，千三百七十四條。

translations.literal: They added another thirty juan and one thousand three hundred and seventy-four articles.
translations.idiomatic: They added another thirty scrolls and 1,374 articles.

sentences.zh: 又有《農田敕》五卷，與敕兼行。

translations.literal: There was also the Farmland Edicts in five juan, applied together with the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Farmland Edicts in five scrolls, enforced alongside the main edicts.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗問輔臣曰：「或謂先朝詔令不可輕改，信然乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong once asked his chief ministers: "Some say that edicts of the former court must not be lightly changed—is that so?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong once asked his chief ministers, "Some say the previous reign's edicts must not be lightly altered—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 王曾曰：「此憸人惑上之言也。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng said: "These are words by crafty men to mislead Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng replied, "That is the talk of crafty men trying to mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 咸平之所刪，太宗詔令十存一二，去其繁密以便於民，何為不可？」

translations.literal: What was deleted in Xianping left only one or two in ten of Taizong's edicts, removing what was dense and intricate to benefit the people—why may that not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xianping revision kept only one or two in ten of Taizong's edicts, cutting away dense and intricate provisions to benefit the people—why should that not be done?"

sentences.zh: 於是詔中外言敕得失，命官修定，取咸平儀制令及制度約束之在敕者五百餘條，悉附令後，號曰《附令敕》。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered officials within and without the court to speak on the strengths and faults of the edicts, and officials were appointed to revise them. More than five hundred articles from the Xianping Ceremonial Regulations Ordinance and institutional constraints that had been in the edicts were all appended after the ordinances, titled Attached Ordinance Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The court then invited comment empire-wide on the edicts' strengths and faults and appointed officials to revise them. More than five hundred articles from the Xianping ceremonial ordinances and institutional rules that had stood in the edicts were appended to the ordinances and titled the Attached Ordinance Edicts.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年編敕成，合《農田敕》為一書，視祥符敕損百有餘條。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiansheng the compiled edicts were completed, the Farmland Edicts merged into one book, and more than one hundred articles were reduced compared with the Xiangfu edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tiansheng the compiled edicts were finished, the Farmland Edicts were merged into a single work, and more than a hundred articles were cut compared with the Xiangfu code.

sentences.zh: 其麗于法者，大辟之屬十有七，流之屬三十有四，徒之屬百有六，杖之屬二百五十有八，笞之屬七十有六。

translations.literal: Those attached to the statutes included seventeen kinds of capital punishment, thirty-four of exile, one hundred and six of penal servitude, two hundred and fifty-eight of beating with the staff, and seventy-six of beating with the light stick.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties tied to the statutes included 17 capital offenses, 34 exile offenses, 106 penal-servitude offenses, 258 staff-beatings, and 76 light-stick beatings.

sentences.zh: 又配隸之屬六十有三，大辟而下奏聽旨者七十有一。

translations.literal: There were also sixty-three kinds of assigned service, and seventy-one cases from capital punishment downward requiring memorial and imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: There were also 63 kinds of assigned labor, and 71 offenses from capital punishment downward that required memorial and imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 凡此，皆在律令外者也。

translations.literal: All these lay outside the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: All of these lay outside the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 既頒行，因下詔曰：「敕令者，治世之經，而數動搖，則眾聽滋惑，何以訓迪天下哉？

translations.literal: After promulgation, an edict was issued saying: "Edicts and ordinances are the warp of a well-governed age; if they are shaken again and again, the multitude grows ever more confused—how may the realm be instructed?
translations.idiomatic: After promulgation the court issued an edict: "Edicts and ordinances are the warp of good government; if they are constantly shaken, the people grow confused—how can the realm be instructed?

sentences.zh: 自今有司毋得輒請刪改。

translations.literal: From now on officials must not on their own request deletion or revision.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth officials must not on their own request deletions or revisions.

sentences.zh: 有未便者，中書、樞密院以聞。」

translations.literal: If something is inconvenient, the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs shall report it."
translations.idiomatic: If anything proves inconvenient, the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs shall report it."

sentences.zh: 然至慶曆又復刪定，增五百條，別為《總例》一卷。

translations.literal: Yet by Qingli they revised again, adding five hundred articles and separately making the General Principles in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by the Qingli era they revised again, adding five hundred articles and issuing a separate scroll of General Principles.

sentences.zh: 後又修一司敕二千三百十有七條，一路敕千八百二十有七條，一州、一縣敕千四百五十有一條。

translations.literal: Later they also revised bureau edicts to two thousand three hundred and seventeen articles, circuit edicts to one thousand eight hundred and twenty-seven, and prefectural and county edicts to one thousand four hundred and fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Later they also revised bureau edicts to 2,317 articles, circuit edicts to 1,827, and prefectural and county edicts to 1,451.

sentences.zh: 其麗于法者，大辟之屬總三十有一，流之屬總二十有一，徒之屬總百有五，杖之屬總百六十有八，笞之屬總十有二，又配隸之屬總八十有一，大辟而下奏聽旨者總六十有四。

translations.literal: Those attached to the statutes totaled thirty-one capital offenses, twenty-one exile offenses, one hundred and five penal servitude, one hundred and sixty-eight staff beatings, twelve light-stick beatings, eighty-one assigned service, and sixty-four from capital punishment downward requiring memorial and imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties tied to the statutes totaled 31 capital offenses, 21 exile offenses, 105 penal servitude, 168 staff beatings, 12 light-stick beatings, 81 assigned labor, and 64 offenses from capital punishment downward requiring memorial and imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 凡此，又在編敕之外者也。

translations.literal: All these again lay outside the compiled edicts.
translations.idiomatic: All of these again lay outside the compiled edicts.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，因樞密使韓琦言，內外吏兵奉祿無著令，乃命類次為祿令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiayou, because Military Affairs Commissioner Han Qi said that salaries for civil and military officials within and without the court had no fixed ordinance, an order was given to classify and compile a Salary Ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiayou reign, after Military Affairs Commissioner Han Qi observed that salaries for officials and soldiers had no fixed ordinance, the court ordered them classified into a Salary Ordinance.

sentences.zh: 三司以驛料名數，著為驛令。

translations.literal: The Three Departments set out the names and amounts of relay-station supplies and made them the Relay Ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments codified relay-station supplies and amounts as the Relay Ordinance.

sentences.zh: 琦又言：「自慶曆四年，距嘉祐二年，敕增至四千餘條，前後牴牾。

translations.literal: Qi also said: "From the fourth year of Qingli to the second year of Jiayou, edicts increased to more than four thousand articles, contradicting one another before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also said, "From the fourth year of Qingli to the second year of Jiayou, edicts grew to more than four thousand articles, often contradicting one another.

sentences.zh: 請詔中外，使言敕得失，如天聖故事。」

translations.literal: I request an edict to officials within and without the court to speak on the strengths and faults of the edicts, as in the Tiansheng precedent."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court, as in the Tiansheng precedent, invite comment empire-wide on the edicts' strengths and faults."

sentences.zh: 七年，書成。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the compilation was finished.

sentences.zh: 總千八百三十四條，視慶曆敕大辟增六十，流增五十，徒增六十有一，杖增七十有三，笞增三十有八，又配隸增三十，大辟而下奏聽旨者增四十有六。

translations.literal: Altogether one thousand eight hundred and thirty-four articles; compared with the Qingli edicts, capital punishment increased by sixty, exile by fifty, penal servitude by sixty-one, staff beating by seventy-three, light stick by thirty-eight, assigned service by thirty, and memorial cases from capital punishment downward by forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether 1,834 articles; compared with the Qingli code, capital offenses rose by 60, exile by 50, penal servitude by 61, staff beatings by 73, light-stick beatings by 38, assigned labor by 30, and memorial cases from capital punishment downward by 46.

sentences.zh: 又別為《續附令敕》三卷。

translations.literal: They also separately made the Continued Attached Ordinance Edicts in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: They also issued the Continued Attached Ordinance Edicts in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 神宗以律不足以周事情，凡律所不載者一斷以敕，乃更其目曰敕、令、格、式，而律恆存乎敕之外。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong held that statutes were insufficient to cover all affairs; whatever the statutes did not record was entirely decided by edict. He then changed the categories to edict, ordinance, regulation, and form, while the statutes always remained outside the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong held that statutes could not cover every circumstance; whatever the statutes omitted was to be decided solely by edict. He reorganized the categories as edicts, ordinances, regulations, and forms, while the statutes themselves remained subordinate to the edicts.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，置局修敕，詔中外言法不便者，集議更定，擇其可采者賞之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining a bureau was established to revise the edicts; an edict ordered officials within and without to speak on inconvenient points in the law, to assemble for discussion and revision, and to reward those whose proposals could be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining the court set up a bureau to revise the edicts and invited empire-wide comment on inconvenient laws, assembling officials to revise them and rewarding proposals that were adopted.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，始成書二十有六卷，復下二府參訂，然後頒行。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng the book was first completed in twenty-six juan; it was again sent to the Two Departments for joint revision, and only then promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng era the work was first completed in twenty-six scrolls, sent to the Two Departments for joint revision, and only then promulgated.

sentences.zh: 帝留意法令，每有司進擬，多所是正。

translations.literal: The emperor paid close attention to statutes and edicts; whenever officials submitted drafts, he often corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid close attention to law; whenever officials submitted drafts, he often corrected them himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「法出於道，人能體道，則立法足以盡事。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Law proceeds from the Way; if people can embody the Way, then legislation suffices to exhaust affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Law proceeds from the Way; if people can embody the Way, legislation alone can cover every affair."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「禁於已然之謂敕，禁於未然之謂令，設於此以待彼之謂格，使彼效之之謂式。

translations.literal: He also said: "What forbids what has already occurred is called edict; what forbids what has not yet occurred is called ordinance; what is set here to await that there is called regulation; what makes the other emulate it is called form.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "What forbids what has already happened is an edict; what forbids what has not yet happened is an ordinance; what is set here to await action there is a regulation; what makes others emulate it is a form.

sentences.zh: 修書者要當識此。」

translations.literal: Those who compile books must understand this."
translations.idiomatic: Compilers must grasp this distinction."

sentences.zh: 於是凡入笞、杖、徒、流、死，自名例以下至斷獄，十有二門，麗刑名輕重者，皆為敕。

translations.literal: Thereupon all matters entering the categories of light stick, staff, penal servitude, exile, and death—from General Principles down to Trial and Judgment, twelve sections in all—whatever concerned the severity of punishments, were all made edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon everything from light-stick beating through staff beating, penal servitude, exile, and death—from General Principles through Trial and Judgment, twelve sections in all—whatever concerned the severity of punishment was classified as edict.

sentences.zh: 自品官以下至斷獄三十五門，約束禁止者，皆為令。

translations.literal: From ranked officials down to Trial and Judgment, thirty-five sections—whatever constrained and forbade—were all made ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: From ranked officials through Trial and Judgment, thirty-five sections—whatever constrained or forbade conduct—were classified as ordinances.

sentences.zh: 命官之等十有七，吏、庶人之賞等七十有七，又有倍、全、分、釐之級凡五等，有等級高下者，皆為格。

translations.literal: Seventeen grades for commissioned officials, seventy-seven reward grades for clerks and commoners, and five levels of double, full, fractional, and minute shares—whatever had higher and lower grades—were all made regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen grades for commissioned officials, seventy-seven reward grades for clerks and commoners, and five levels of double, full, fractional, and minute shares—whatever involved graded distinctions—were classified as regulations.

sentences.zh: 表奏、帳籍、關牒、符檄之類凡五卷，有體制模楷者，皆為式。

translations.literal: Memorials, registers, passes, and dispatches and the like, five juan in all—whatever had formal models—were all made forms.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials, registers, passes, and dispatches and the like, five scrolls in all—whatever had prescribed formats—were classified as forms.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，中丞劉摯言：「元豐編修敕令，舊載敕者多移之令，蓋違敕法重，違令罪輕，此足以見神宗仁厚之德。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi said: "In the Yuanfeng revision of edicts and ordinances, many matters formerly recorded as edicts were moved to ordinances, because violating an edict was severe while violating an ordinance was light—this suffices to show Emperor Shenzong's benevolent and generous virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi said, "In the Yuanfeng revision, many provisions formerly classified as edicts were moved to ordinances, because violating an edict carried heavier penalties than violating an ordinance—enough to show Emperor Shenzong's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 而有司不能推廣，增多條目，離析舊制，因一言一事，輒立一法，意苛文晦，不足以該事物之情。

translations.literal: Yet the officials could not extend this, multiplying articles, splitting apart old institutions, and for a single word or affair immediately establishing a law—intent harsh, text obscure, insufficient to encompass the circumstances of things.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials failed to extend that spirit: they multiplied articles, fragmented old institutions, and for every word or incident promptly enacted a new rule—harsh in intent, obscure in wording, unable to cover real circumstances.

sentences.zh: 行之幾時，蓋已屢變。

translations.literal: After it had been in force only a short while, it had already changed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short time it had already been changed again and again.

sentences.zh: 宜取慶曆、嘉祐以來新舊敕參照，去取刪正，以成一代之典。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to take the old and new edicts from Qingli and Jiayou onward for comparison, selecting and deleting to correct them, to complete the canon of a generation."
translations.idiomatic: The court should compare old and new edicts from Qingli and Jiayou onward, revise them by selection and deletion, and complete the code of the age."

sentences.zh: 右諫議孫覺亦言煩細難以檢用，乃詔摯等刊定。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Adviser Sun Jue also said they were so detailed as to be hard to consult and apply, whereupon an edict ordered Liu Zhi and others to revise them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Adviser Sun Jue also complained that the code had grown too detailed to use, and the court ordered Liu Zhi and others to revise it.

sentences.zh: 哲宗親政，不專用元祐近例，稍復熙寧、元豐之制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong personally took power, he did not rely solely on recent Yuanyou precedents but gradually restored the institutions of Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong took personal rule, he no longer relied solely on recent Yuanyou precedents but gradually restored Xining and Yuanfeng institutions.

sentences.zh: 自是用法以後衝前，改更紛然，而刑制紊矣。

translations.literal: From then on in applying the law, later provisions overrode earlier ones; revisions piled up in confusion, and the penal system fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From then on later provisions constantly overrode earlier ones, revisions multiplied in confusion, and the penal system fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 高宗播遷，斷例散逸，建炎以前，凡所施行，類出人吏省記。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was driven into exile, precedent cases were scattered and lost; before Jianyan, whatever was put into practice mostly came from clerks' private memoranda.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong fled south, precedent cases were scattered and lost; before Jianyan, whatever was enforced mostly came from clerks' private notes.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，始命取嘉祐條法與政和敕令對修而用之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, an order was first given to take the Jiayou articles of law and the Zhenghe edicts and ordinances, revise them against each other, and use them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year the court first ordered the Jiayou code and the Zhenghe edicts revised against each other and put into use.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐法與見行不同者，自官制、役法外，賞格從重，條約從輕。

translations.literal: Where the Jiayou law differed from what was currently in force, apart from the official system and labor-service law, reward scales followed the heavier and treaty provisions the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Jiayou code differed from current practice, except for the official system and labor-service laws, reward scales followed the stricter version and treaty provisions the lighter.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，書成，號《紹興敕令格式》，而吏胥省記者亦復引用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing the book was completed, titled Shaoxing Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms, yet clerks again cited their private memoranda.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing the compilation was finished as the Shaoxing Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms, yet clerks again cited their private notes.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劉一止言：「法令具在，吏猶得以為姦，今一切用其所省記，欺蔽何所不至！」

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Liu Yizhi said: "The laws and edicts are all in place, yet clerks can still commit fraud; now if everything relies on their private memoranda, what deception will not be reached!"
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Liu Yizhi said, "The laws are all on the books, yet clerks still commit fraud; if everything now relies on their private notes, what deception will they not attempt!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，乃詔左右司、敕令所刊定省記之文頒之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict ordered the Left and Right Offices and the Edict Bureau to revise the memoranda texts and promulgate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court ordered the Left and Right Offices and the Edict Bureau to revise the memoranda and promulgate them.

sentences.zh: 時在京通用敕內，有已嘗衝改不該引用之文，因大理正張柄言，亦詔刪削。

translations.literal: At the time, within the edicts commonly used in the capital, there were passages that had already been superseded and ought not to be cited; because Court of Judicial Review Rectifier Zhang Bing spoke on this, an edict also ordered them deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Among the edicts commonly used in the capital were passages already superseded and unfit for citation; after Rectifier Zhang Bing of the Court of Judicial Review spoke up, the court ordered them deleted.

sentences.zh: 十年，右僕射秦檜上之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Right Vice Director Qin Hui presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Right Vice Director Qin Hui presented the work to the throne.

sentences.zh: 然自檜專政，率用都堂批狀、指揮行事，雜入吏部續降條冊之中，修書者有所畏忌，不敢刪削，至與成法並立。

translations.literal: Yet from the time Qin monopolized power, he routinely used Grand Council rescripts and directives to conduct affairs, mixing them into the Ministry of Personnel's continuing registers of articles; compilers were afraid and dared not delete them, until they stood alongside established law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once Qin dominated the government, he routinely governed by Grand Council rescripts and directives, which were mixed into the Ministry of Personnel's continuing registers; compilers feared him and dared not delete them, until they stood alongside established law.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書周麟之言：「非天子不議禮，不制度，不考文。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhou Lin said: "Only the Son of Heaven deliberates on ritual, establishes institutions, and examines culture."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhou Lin said, "Only the Son of Heaven may deliberate on ritual, establish institutions, and examine culture."

sentences.zh: 乃詔削去之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered them cut away.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered them removed.

sentences.zh: 至乾道時，臣僚言：「紹興以來，續降指揮無慮數千，牴牾難以考據。」

translations.literal: By the Qiandao period officials said: "Since Shaoxing, continuing directives number no fewer than several thousand; they contradict one another and are hard to verify."
translations.idiomatic: By the Qiandao era officials said, "Since Shaoxing, continuing directives number in the thousands; they contradict one another and are impossible to verify."

sentences.zh: 詔大理寺官詳難，定其可否，類申刑部，以所隸事目分送六部長貳參詳。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Court of Judicial Review officials to examine and dispute them, fix what was acceptable or not, classify and report to the Ministry of Justice, and according to the subject matter send them to the chief and vice ministers of the Six Ministries for joint review.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Court of Judicial Review officials to examine them, decide what was acceptable, classify them for the Ministry of Justice, and send each subject to the heads of the Six Ministries for joint review.

sentences.zh: 六年，刑部侍郎汪大猷等上其書，號《乾道敕令格式》，八年，頒之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Vice Minister of Justice Wang Dayou and others presented the book, titled Qiandao Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms; in the eighth year it was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Vice Minister Wang Dayou of the Ministry of Justice and others presented the work as the Qiandao Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms; it was promulgated in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 當是時，法令雖具，然吏一切以例從事，法當然而無例，則事 皆泥而不行，甚至隱例以壞法，賄賂既行，乃為具例。

translations.literal: At that time, although laws and edicts were complete, clerks handled everything by precedent alone; when the law required something but there was no precedent, affairs all stuck fast and could not proceed—even concealing precedents to ruin the law, and only after bribes were paid preparing the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, though the laws were complete, clerks handled everything by precedent; when the law required action but no precedent existed, business stalled entirely—some even concealed precedents to subvert the law, preparing a precedent only after a bribe was paid.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，詔除刑部許用乾道刑名斷例，司勳許用獲盜推賞例，?乾道經置條例事指揮，其餘並不得引例。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, an edict made exceptions: the Ministry of Justice was permitted to use Qiandao criminal-name precedent cases, the Ministry of Personnel was permitted to use reward precedents for catching thieves, and Qiandao special regulations on matters and directives; all others were forbidden to cite precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunxi an edict permitted only three exceptions to the ban on citing precedent: the Ministry of Justice might use Qiandao criminal precedent cases, the Ministry of Personnel might use reward precedents for catching thieves, and Qiandao special regulations and matter directives; all other citation of precedent was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 既而臣僚言乾道新書，尚多牴牾，詔戶部尚書蔡洸詳定之，凡刪改九百餘條，號《淳熙敕令格式》。

translations.literal: Soon officials said the Qiandao new book still contained many contradictions; an edict ordered Minister of Revenue Cai Guang to examine and fix it, deleting and revising more than nine hundred articles in all, titled Chunxi Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon officials complained that the Qiandao code still contained many contradictions; the court ordered Minister of Revenue Cai Guang to revise it, deleting and altering more than nine hundred articles, and titled the result the Chunxi Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.

sentences.zh: 帝復以其書散漫，用法之際，官不暇徧閱，吏因得以容姦，令敕令所分門編類為一書，名曰《淳熙條法事類》，前此法令之所未有也。

translations.literal: The emperor again found the book scattered; when applying the law, officials had no time to read it all, and clerks thus found room for fraud. He ordered the Edict Bureau to arrange it by categories into one book, named Chunxi Classified Articles of Law by Subject—something previous codes had not had.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found the code too scattered: officials could not read it all when applying the law, and clerks exploited the gaps. He ordered the Edict Bureau to arrange it by subject in a single work, the Chunxi Classified Articles of Law by Subject—something no earlier code had attempted.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，頒之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year it was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: It was promulgated in the seventh month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 淳熙末，議者猶以新書尚多遺闕，有司引用，間有便於人情者。

translations.literal: Late in Chunxi, critics still held that the new book had many omissions; when officials cited it, there were occasionally provisions convenient to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Chunxi critics still held that the new code had many gaps; when officials cited it, they sometimes found provisions that suited human sentiment better than the code.

sentences.zh: 復令刑部詳定，迄光宗之世未成。

translations.literal: They again ordered the Ministry of Justice to examine and fix it, but by the age of Emperor Guangzong it was still not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered the Ministry of Justice to revise it, but the work was still unfinished by the reign of Emperor Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 慶元四年，右丞相京鏜始上其書，為百二十卷，號《慶元敕令格式》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingyuan Right Chancellor Jing Tang first presented the book, one hundred and twenty juan, titled Qingyuan Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingyuan Right Chancellor Jing Tang first presented the work in 120 scrolls as the Qingyuan Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.

sentences.zh: 理宗寶慶初，敕令所言：「自慶元新書之行，今二十九年，前指揮殆非一事，或舊法該括未盡，文意未明，須用續降參酌者；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baqing under Emperor Lizong, the Edict Bureau said: "Since the Qingyuan new book was issued, twenty-nine years have now passed; earlier directives are hardly a single matter—some old laws do not fully cover cases, the wording is unclear, and continuing directives must be consulted;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baqing under Emperor Lizong, the Edict Bureau reported, "Twenty-nine years have passed since the Qingyuan code was issued; earlier directives are innumerable—some old laws do not fully cover cases, the wording is unclear, and continuing directives must be consulted;

sentences.zh: 或舊法元無，而後因事立為成法者；

translations.literal: some old laws originally had no provision, but later because of affairs they were established as standing law;
translations.idiomatic: some matters had no old law but later became standing law because of events;

sentences.zh: 或已有舊法，而續降不必引用者；

translations.literal: some already had old law, but continuing directives need not be cited;
translations.idiomatic: some already had old law and need not cite continuing directives;

sentences.zh: 或一時權宜，而不可為常法者。

translations.literal: some were temporary expedients and cannot serve as standing law.
translations.idiomatic: some were temporary expedients unfit to serve as standing law.

sentences.zh: 條目滋繁，無所遵守，乞攷定之。」

translations.literal: Articles grow ever more numerous with nothing to follow—we beg that they be examined and fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Articles have multiplied until nothing can be followed—we beg that they be examined and revised."

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年四月，敕令所上其書，名《淳祐敕令格式》。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Chunyou the Edict Bureau presented the book, named Chunyou Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Chunyou the Edict Bureau presented the Chunyou Edicts, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又取慶元法與淳祐新書刪潤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year they again took the Qingyuan law and the Chunyou new book, deleting and polishing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they again revised the Qingyuan code and the Chunyou new book by deletion and polish.

sentences.zh: 其間修改者百四十條，創入者四百條，增入者五十條，刪去者十七條，為四百三十卷。

translations.literal: Among them one hundred and forty articles were revised, four hundred newly entered, fifty added, seventeen deleted, four hundred and thirty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: They revised 140 articles, added 400 new ones, supplemented 50, deleted 17, and produced 430 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 度宗以後，遵而行之，無所更定矣。

translations.literal: After Emperor Duzong they followed and applied it without further revision.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Duzong the court followed it without further revision.

sentences.zh: 其餘一司、一路、一州、一縣敕，前後時有增損，不可勝紀云。

translations.literal: As for the remaining bureau, circuit, prefectural, and county edicts, additions and reductions occurred from time to time before and after, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: As for bureau, circuit, prefectural, and county edicts, additions and reductions over time are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 五季衰亂，禁罔煩密。

translations.literal: In the decline and chaos of the Five Dynasties, prohibitions and nets were numerous and intricate.
translations.idiomatic: During the decline and chaos of the Five Dynasties, prohibitions were numerous and intricate.

sentences.zh: 宋興，削除苛峻，累朝有所更定。

translations.literal: When the Song arose, harsh and severe provisions were removed, and successive reigns made revisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song arose, harsh provisions were removed, and successive reigns revised the code.

sentences.zh: 法吏寖用儒臣，務存仁恕，凡用法不悖而宜于時者著之。

translations.literal: Legal officials gradually employed Confucian ministers, striving to preserve benevolence and forgiveness; whatever in applying the law was not contrary and suited the times is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Legal offices gradually drew on Confucian scholars, striving to preserve benevolence and leniency; whatever in the application of law was sound and suited the times is recorded here.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，始定折杖之制。

translations.literal: When the Taizu received the abdication, he first established the system of commuted beatings.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu accepted the throne, he first established the system of commuted corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 凡流刑四：加役流，脊杖二十，配役三年；

translations.literal: There were four types of exile punishment: augmented labor exile, twenty strokes on the back, and three years of assigned labor service;
translations.idiomatic: Exile punishments numbered four: augmented labor exile carried twenty strokes on the back and three years of assigned labor;

sentences.zh: 流三千里，脊杖二十，二千五百里，脊杖十八，二千里，脊杖十七，並配役一年。

translations.literal: Exile three thousand li, twenty strokes on the back; two thousand five hundred li, eighteen strokes on the back; two thousand li, seventeen strokes on the back—all with one year of assigned labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to three thousand li meant twenty strokes on the back; to two thousand five hundred li, eighteen strokes; to two thousand li, seventeen strokes—all with one year of assigned labor.

sentences.zh: 凡徒刑五：徒三年，脊杖二十；

translations.literal: There were five types of penal servitude: three years' servitude, twenty strokes on the back;
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude had five grades: three years' servitude brought twenty strokes on the back;

sentences.zh: 徒二年半，脊杖十八；

translations.literal: Two and a half years' servitude, eighteen strokes on the back;
translations.idiomatic: Two and a half years' servitude, eighteen strokes on the back;

sentences.zh: 二年，脊杖十七；

translations.literal: Two years, seventeen strokes on the back;
translations.idiomatic: Two years, seventeen strokes on the back;

sentences.zh: 一年半，脊杖十五；

translations.literal: One and a half years, fifteen strokes on the back;
translations.idiomatic: One and a half years, fifteen strokes on the back;

sentences.zh: 一年，脊杖十三。

translations.literal: One year, thirteen strokes on the back.
translations.idiomatic: One year, thirteen strokes on the back.

sentences.zh: 凡杖刑五：杖一百，臀杖二十；

translations.literal: There were five types of staff beating: one hundred strokes of the staff, twenty strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Staff beatings had five grades: a sentence of one hundred strokes meant twenty strokes on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 九十，臀杖十八；

translations.literal: Ninety strokes, eighteen strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Ninety strokes, eighteen on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 八十，臀杖十七；

translations.literal: Eighty strokes, seventeen strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Eighty strokes, seventeen on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 七十，臀杖十五；

translations.literal: Seventy strokes, fifteen strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Seventy strokes, fifteen on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 六十，臀杖十三。

translations.literal: Sixty strokes, thirteen strokes on the buttocks.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty strokes, thirteen on the buttocks.

sentences.zh: 凡笞刑五：笞五十，臀杖十下；

translations.literal: There were five types of whipping: fifty strokes of the whip, ten strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Whipping punishments had five grades: fifty strokes meant ten blows on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 四十、三十，臀杖八下；

translations.literal: Forty and thirty strokes, eight strokes on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: Forty and thirty strokes, eight blows on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 二十、十，臀杖七下。

translations.literal: Twenty and ten strokes, seven strokes on the buttocks.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty and ten strokes, seven blows on the buttocks.

sentences.zh: 常行官杖如周顯德五年制，長三尺五寸，大頭闊不過二寸，厚及小頭徑不得過九分。

translations.literal: The standard administrative staff followed the system of the fifth year of Xiande under Zhou: three feet five inches long, the broad end no more than two inches wide, and the thickness and diameter of the narrow end no more than nine tenths of an inch.
translations.idiomatic: The standard beating staff followed the Zhou Xiande 5 regulations: three feet five inches long, no more than two inches across at the broad end, and no more than nine tenths of an inch thick or in diameter at the narrow end.

sentences.zh: 徒、流、笞通用常行杖，徒罪決而不役。

translations.literal: Penal servitude, exile, and whipping all used the standard staff; for servitude offenses the beating was carried out but labor service was not imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude, exile, and whipping all used the standard staff; for servitude offenses the beating was administered but labor service was waived.

sentences.zh: 先是，藩鎮跋扈，專殺為威，朝廷姑息，率置不問，刑部按覆之職廢矣。

translations.literal: Previously, the military governors were overbearing, making arbitrary killing their instrument of intimidation; the court indulged them and generally let matters pass without inquiry, and the Ministry of Justice's duty of review was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, military governors had grown overbearing, wielding arbitrary execution as a threat; the court indulged them and generally looked the other way, and the Ministry of Justice's review function fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，令諸州奏大辟案，須刑部詳覆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, an order was issued that when the various prefectures reported capital cases, the Ministry of Justice had to conduct a detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 3, an edict required all prefectures reporting capital cases to submit them for detailed review by the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋如舊制，大理寺詳斷，而後覆于刑部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the old system was restored: the Court of Judicial Review would examine and decide cases, and then they would be reviewed by the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the old procedure was restored: the Court of Judicial Review would examine and decide cases, which were then reviewed by the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州獄，則錄事參軍與司法掾參斷之。

translations.literal: For all prison cases in the prefectures, the recording secretary and the judicial clerk jointly adjudicated them.
translations.idiomatic: In prefectural prisons, the recording secretary and the judicial clerk jointly adjudicated cases.

sentences.zh: 自是，內外折獄蔽罪，皆有官以相覆察。

translations.literal: From this time on, whether inside or outside the capital, in trying cases and concealing crimes, there were officials to review and inspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whether at court or in the provinces, trial and concealment of offenses were subject to mutual review by designated officials.

sentences.zh: 又懼刑部、大理寺用法之失，別置審刑院讞之。

translations.literal: Fearing further errors in the application of law by the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review, a separate Office of Reviewing Punishments was established to deliberate on cases.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing further misapplication of the law by the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review, a separate Office of Reviewing Punishments was established to review verdicts.

sentences.zh: 吏一坐深，或終身不進，由是皆務持平。

translations.literal: If an official once received a heavy sentence, he might never advance for the rest of his life; because of this, all strove to be even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: An official who once received a severe penalty might never advance again; from then on, all strove to hold the middle ground.

sentences.zh: 唐建中令，竊盜贓滿三匹者死。

translations.literal: Under the Jianzhong edict of Tang, theft of booty amounting to three bolts of cloth was punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang's Jianzhong edict, theft of goods worth three bolts of cloth or more was capital.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，竊盜贓滿千錢者死。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wuzong, theft of booty amounting to one thousand cash was punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wuzong, theft of one thousand cash or more was capital.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，乃罷之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, the provision was abolished.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐以來，用法益峻，民盜一錢抵極法。

translations.literal: From the Qianyou era of Han onward, the application of law grew ever harsher, and a commoner who stole one cash faced the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: From the Later Han Qianyou era onward, the law grew ever harsher—a commoner who stole a single coin could face the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 周初，深懲其失，復遵建中之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou, deeply correcting this error, they again followed the Jianzhong system.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou dynasty, deeply regretting this excess, the court restored the Jianzhong standard.

sentences.zh: 帝猶以其太重，嘗增為錢三千，陌以八十為限。

translations.literal: The emperor still considered it too severe and once raised the threshold to three thousand cash, with a string counted at eighty as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still found it too harsh and once raised the threshold to three thousand cash, counting a full string at eighty coins.

sentences.zh: 既而詔曰：「禁民為非，乃設法令，臨下以簡，必務哀矜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an edict said: "To restrain the people from wrongdoing, laws and ordinances are established; in governing those below, simplicity must be maintained, and compassion must be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict declared: "Laws exist to restrain the people from wrongdoing; in governing those below, keep matters simple and always show compassion.

sentences.zh: 竊盜之生，本非巨 。

translations.literal: The offense of theft by nature is not a grave crime.
translations.idiomatic: Petty theft by its nature is not a grave crime.

sentences.zh: 近朝立制，重於律文，非愛人之旨也。

translations.literal: The regulations established in recent dynasties were heavier than the text of the code—this is not the intent of caring for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Recent dynasties had set penalties heavier than the code itself—hardly the spirit of caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 自今竊盜贓滿五貫足陌者死。」

translations.literal: From now on, theft of booty amounting to five strings of full denomination shall be punishable by death."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, theft of five full strings of cash or more shall be capital."

sentences.zh: 舊法，強盜持杖，雖不傷人，皆棄市。

translations.literal: Under the old law, armed robbers who carried staffs, even if they did not injure anyone, were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, armed robbers were executed in the marketplace even when no one was harmed.

sentences.zh: 又詔但不傷人者，止計贓論。

translations.literal: Another edict provided that when no one was injured, punishment was determined solely by the value of the booty.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict provided that when no one was injured, the penalty was determined solely by the value of the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 令諸州獲盜，非狀驗明白，未得掠治。

translations.literal: An order was issued that when the various prefectures apprehended thieves, unless the facts were clearly verified, torture to extract confession was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were ordered not to torture captured thieves unless the facts had been clearly established.

sentences.zh: 其當訊者，先具白長吏，得判乃訊之。

translations.literal: Those who were to be interrogated had first to submit a report to the chief official; only after receiving his written approval could they be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: When interrogation was required, officials had first to report to the chief magistrate and could question the prisoner only after receiving written approval.

sentences.zh: 凡有司擅掠囚者，論為私罪。

translations.literal: Whenever officials on their own authority tortured prisoners, it was treated as a private offense.
translations.idiomatic: Any official who tortured prisoners without authorization was charged with a private offense.

sentences.zh: 時天下甫定，刑典弛廢，吏不明習律令，牧守又多武人，率意用法。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had only just been pacified; the penal code had fallen into disuse; officials were not well versed in statutes and ordinances; and many prefects and governors were military men who applied the law as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had only just been pacified; the penal code had fallen into neglect; officials were poorly versed in statutes; and many prefects and governors were military men who applied the law as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 金州防禦使仇超等坐故入死罪，除名，流海島，自是人知奉法矣。

translations.literal: Qiu Chao, defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture, and others were convicted of deliberately imposing the death penalty, stripped of their names, and exiled to island penal colonies; from then on people knew to obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Chao, defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture, and others were convicted of deliberately imposing capital punishment, stripped of rank, and exiled to island penal colonies; from then on, people understood they must obey the law.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年五月，帝以暑氣方盛，深念縲繫之苦，乃下手詔：「兩京諸州，令長吏督獄掾，五日一檢視，洒掃獄戶，洗滌杻械。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaibao, the emperor, because the heat was at its height, deeply mindful of the suffering of those bound in fetters, personally issued an edict: "In the two capitals and all prefectures, let the chief officials supervise the prison clerks to inspect the prisons every five days, sweep the prison gates, and wash the shackles and instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaibao 2, with summer heat at its peak, the emperor, deeply mindful of the suffering of the imprisoned, personally issued an edict: "In the two capitals and all prefectures, chief officials shall supervise prison clerks in inspecting the jails every five days, sweeping the gates, and washing shackles and restraints.

sentences.zh: 貧不能自存者給飲食，病者給醫藥，輕繫即時決遣，毋淹滯。」

translations.literal: Those too poor to support themselves were given food and drink; the sick were given medicine; those held on minor charges were promptly decided and released, without delay."
translations.idiomatic: The destitute were to receive food and drink; the sick, medicine; those held on minor charges were to be tried and released at once, without delay."

sentences.zh: 自是，每仲夏申敕官吏，歲以為常。

translations.literal: From this time on, every midsummer officials were admonished in an edict, and this became an annual practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, every midsummer officials received such admonitions, and the practice became annual.

sentences.zh: 帝每親錄囚徒，專事欽恤。

translations.literal: The emperor personally reviewed prisoners every year, devoting himself entirely to compassionate consideration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally reviewed prisoners each year, devoting himself entirely to compassionate judgment.

sentences.zh: 凡御史、大理官屬，尤嚴選擇。

translations.literal: Officials of the Censorate and the Court of Judicial Review were especially strictly selected.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Censorate and the Court of Judicial Review were chosen with particular care.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂侍御史知雜馮炳曰：「朕每讀《漢書》，見張釋之、于定國治獄，天下無民，此所望於卿也。」

translations.literal: He once said to the supervising censor Feng Bing: "Whenever I read the Book of Han and see how Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo handled prisons so that no one in the realm suffered wrongful conviction, this is what I hope for from you."
translations.idiomatic: He once told the supervising censor Feng Bing: "When I read the Book of Han and see how Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo presided over the courts so that no one in the realm suffered wrongful conviction, that is what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 賜金紫以勉之。

translations.literal: He bestowed gold and purple insignia to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed gold and purple insignia to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 八年，廣州言：「前詔竊盜贓至死者奏裁，嶺南遐遠，覆奏稽滯，請不俟報。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Guangzhou reported: "The earlier edict required that capital cases of theft be submitted for imperial decision; Lingnan is remote and far away, and the delay in reporting back is prolonged—we request not to wait for a reply."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Guangzhou reported: "The earlier edict required capital theft cases to be submitted for imperial approval; Lingnan is remote, and the round of review causes long delays—we ask permission to proceed without awaiting a reply."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，惻然曰：「海隅習俗，貪獷穿窬，固其常也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, he said with compassion: "The customs of the coastal regions—greed and burglary through holes in walls—are naturally so."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor said with compassion: "In the coastal south, greed and petty burglary are simply the way of things."

sentences.zh: 因詔：「嶺南民犯竊盜，贓滿五貫至十貫者，決杖、黥面、配役，十貫以上乃死。」

translations.literal: He then issued an edict: "When the people of Lingnan commit theft, if the booty amounts from five to ten strings, they shall receive beating, facial tattooing, and assigned labor service; only when it exceeds ten strings shall they be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: He then decreed: "For theft in Lingnan, booty of five to ten strings shall bring beating, facial tattooing, and assigned labor; only amounts above ten strings shall be capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗在御，常躬聽斷，在京獄有疑者，多臨決之，每能燭見隱微。

translations.literal: When Taizong held the throne, he often personally heard and decided cases; when there were doubtful cases in the capital prisons, he frequently decided them in person and could always discern what was hidden and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong reigned, he often heard cases in person; doubtful cases in the capital prisons he frequently decided himself, and he could always see through what was hidden.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年下詔曰：「諸州大獄，長吏不親決，胥吏旁緣為姦，逮捕證佐，滋蔓踰年而獄未具。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo an edict was issued: "In major prison cases in the various prefectures, the chief officials do not decide them personally; clerks seize opportunities to commit wrongdoing, arrest witnesses and associates, and cases drag on for more than a year without being completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 6 an edict declared: "In major cases across the prefectures, chief magistrates fail to decide them personally; clerks exploit the gaps to commit abuses, witnesses are arrested, and cases drag on for more than a year without resolution.

sentences.zh: 自今長吏每五日一慮囚，情得者即決之。」

translations.literal: From now on, chief officials shall review prisoners every five days; when the facts are clear, they shall decide the cases at once."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth chief magistrates shall review prisoners every five days and decide cases immediately when the facts are clear."

sentences.zh: 復制聽獄之限，大事四十日，中事二十日，小事十日，不他逮捕而易決者，毋過三日。

translations.literal: Time limits for hearing cases were reinstituted: major cases forty days, medium cases twenty days, minor cases ten days; cases requiring no further arrests and easily decided were not to exceed three days.
translations.idiomatic: Time limits for hearing cases were restored: forty days for major cases, twenty for medium, ten for minor; cases needing no further arrests and easily decided were not to exceed three days.

sentences.zh: 後又定令：「決獄違限，準官書稽程律論，踰四十日則奏裁。

translations.literal: Later a regulation was established: "When deciding cases exceeded the time limit, punishment followed the statute on delay in official documents; if it exceeded forty days, the matter was submitted for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Later a regulation provided: "Exceeding time limits in deciding cases was punishable under the statute on delay in official documents; cases exceeding forty days were submitted for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 事須證逮致稽緩者，所在以其事聞。」

translations.literal: When delay was caused by the need to summon witnesses, the locality was to report the matter."
translations.idiomatic: When delay was caused by the need to summon witnesses, the locality was to report the circumstances."

sentences.zh: 然州縣禁繫，往往猶以根窮為名，追擾輒至破家。

translations.literal: Yet in the prefectures and counties, detention often still went under the name of tracing matters to their roots, and the pursuit and harassment frequently ruined families.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefectures and counties still often detained people under the pretext of tracing cases to their roots, and the pursuit and harassment frequently ruined families.

sentences.zh: 因江西轉運副使張齊賢言，令外縣罪人五日一具禁放數白州。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Zhang Qixian, vice transport commissioner of Jiangxi, an order was issued that outer counties report the numbers of those detained and released every five days to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Zhang Qixian, vice transport commissioner of Jiangxi, outer counties were ordered to report detention and release figures to the prefecture every five days.

sentences.zh: 州獄別置曆，長吏檢察，三五日一引問疏理，月具奏上。

translations.literal: The prefectural prison was to keep a separate register; the chief official was to inspect it, summon and question prisoners every three to five days to sort out their cases, and submit a monthly report.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural prisons were to keep separate registers; chief magistrates were to inspect them, summon and review prisoners every three to five days, and submit monthly reports.

sentences.zh: 刑部閱其禁多者，命官即往決遣，滯則降黜州之官吏。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Justice found excessive numbers detained, it dispatched officials at once to decide and release them; if there was delay, the prefecture's officials were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Justice found excessive detentions, it dispatched officials to decide and release cases at once; delay brought demotion for the prefecture's officials.

sentences.zh: 會兩浙運司亦言：「部內州繫囚滿獄，長吏輒隱落，妄言獄空，蓋懼朝廷詰其淹滯。」

translations.literal: At the same time the transport office of the two Zhe regions also reported: "Prisoners in the prefectures within our jurisdiction fill the jails; chief officials conceal and omit them and falsely claim the prisons are empty, fearing that the court will question their delays."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Two Zhe transport office reported: "Prisoners fill the jails in our prefectures; chief magistrates conceal the numbers and falsely claim empty prisons, fearing the court will question their delays."

sentences.zh: 乃詔：「妄奏獄空及隱落囚數，必加深譴，募告者賞之。」

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "Those who falsely report empty prisons or conceal prisoner numbers shall receive severe punishment; informants shall be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "False reports of empty prisons or concealed prisoner counts would bring severe punishment; informants would be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 開封女子李嘗擊登聞鼓，自言無兒息，身且病，一旦死，家業無所付，詔本府隨所欲裁置之。

translations.literal: A woman of Kaifeng surnamed Li once struck the drum at the Hall for Petitions, saying she had no sons or heirs, was ill, and feared that if she died suddenly her family property would have no one to receive it; an edict ordered the prefecture to dispose of it as she wished.
translations.idiomatic: A Kaifeng woman surnamed Li once struck the petition drum, saying she had no heirs, was ill, and feared that if she died her estate would have no recipient; the court ordered the prefecture to dispose of her property as she wished.

sentences.zh: 李無它親，獨有父，有司因繫之。

translations.literal: Li had no other relatives, only a father; the authorities therefore detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Li had no other kin, only a father; the authorities therefore detained him.

sentences.zh: 李又詣登聞，訴父被縶，帝駭曰：「此事豈當禁繫，輦轂之下，尚或如此。

translations.literal: Li again went to the Hall for Petitions and complained that her father had been bound; the emperor said in alarm: "How could such a matter warrant detention? Under the imperial chariot's hub, such things still occur.
translations.idiomatic: Li returned to the petition hall to complain that her father had been bound; the emperor said in alarm: "How could such a matter warrant detention? Even at the capital, such things still happen.

sentences.zh: 又下至廣，安得無枉濫乎？

translations.literal: And when it reaches down to the broad regions, how could there be no wrongful abuse?
translations.idiomatic: And in the wider realm, how could there be no wrongful abuse?

sentences.zh: 朕恨不能親決四方之獄，固不辭勞爾！」

translations.literal: I regret that I cannot personally decide the prison cases of the four directions—I certainly do not shrink from the labor!"
translations.idiomatic: I regret that I cannot personally decide cases throughout the realm—I certainly do not shrink from the effort!"

sentences.zh: 即日遣殿中侍御史李範等十四人，分往江南、兩浙、四川、荊湖、嶺南審決刑獄。

translations.literal: That same day he dispatched fourteen palace censors including Li Fan to Jiangnan, the two Zhe regions, Sichuan, Jinghu, and Lingnan to examine and decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he dispatched fourteen palace censors including Li Fan to Jiangnan, the Two Zhe, Sichuan, Jinghu, and Lingnan to review and decide criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 吏之怠者，劾其罪以聞；

translations.literal: Officials who were negligent were impeached and their offenses reported;
translations.idiomatic: Negligent officials were impeached and reported;

sentences.zh: 其臨事明敏、刑獄無滯者，亦以名上。

translations.literal: Those who were sharp in handling affairs and kept criminal cases from stagnating were also reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: Those who handled affairs with clarity and kept cases moving were also reported by name for commendation.

sentences.zh: 始令諸州十日一慮囚。

translations.literal: For the first time an order was issued that the various prefectures review prisoners every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time, prefectures were ordered to review prisoners every ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂宰相曰：「御史臺，閤門之前，四方綱準之地。

translations.literal: The emperor once said to the chief ministers: "The Censorate stands before the Gate of the Inner Court—it is the place where the standards of the four directions converge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told the chief ministers: "The Censorate stands before the Inner Court gate—it is where the standards of the entire realm converge.

sentences.zh: 頗聞臺中鞫獄，御史多不躬親，垂簾雍容，以自尊大。

translations.literal: I have often heard that in interrogating cases at the Censorate, many censors do not attend in person but sit behind curtains with an air of ease to magnify their own importance.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in the Censorate's interrogations, many censors do not attend in person but sit behind curtains in stately ease to magnify their own importance.

sentences.zh: 鞫按之任，委在胥吏，求無 濫，豈可得也？」

translations.literal: The duty of interrogation and investigation is entrusted to clerks—how can one seek no wrongful abuse?"
translations.idiomatic: The duty of interrogation is left to clerks—how can one hope to avoid wrongful abuse?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔御史決獄必躬親，毋得專任胥吏。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that censors deciding cases must attend in person and must not leave the task entirely to clerks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed requiring censors to decide cases in person and not leave the work entirely to clerks.

sentences.zh: 又嘗諭宰臣曰：「每閱大理奏案，節目小未備，移文按覆，動涉數千里外，禁繫淹久，甚可憐也。

translations.literal: He also once instructed the chief ministers: "Whenever I review cases submitted by the Court of Judicial Review, if minor details are incomplete, documents are sent back for review, often involving places thousands of li away; detention drags on for long periods—it is deeply pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the chief ministers: "When I review cases from the Court of Judicial Review, if minor details are incomplete, documents are sent back for review—often to places thousands of li away—and detainees languish for long periods. It is deeply pitiable.

sentences.zh: 卿等詳酌，非人命所係，即量罪區分，勿須再鞫。」

translations.literal: You should consider carefully: if human life is not at stake, then distinguish punishments according to the offense and do not require re-interrogation."
translations.idiomatic: Consider carefully: when human life is not at stake, distinguish punishments according to the offense and do not require re-interrogation."

sentences.zh: 始令諸州笞、杖罪不須證逮者，長吏即決之，勿復付所司。

translations.literal: For the first time an order was issued that in the various prefectures, whipping and staff-beating offenses requiring no witnesses to be summoned were to be decided at once by the chief official and not again referred to the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were first ordered that whipping and staff-beating offenses requiring no witnesses were to be decided at once by the chief magistrate, without referral to subordinate offices.

sentences.zh: 羣臣受詔鞫獄，獄既具，騎置來上，有司斷已，復騎置下之州。

translations.literal: When ministers received edicts to interrogate cases, once the cases were complete, courier relays brought them up; after the relevant office had decided them, courier relays sent them back down to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers received edicts to interrogate cases, completed dossiers were sent up by courier relay; after the relevant office decided them, couriers relayed the verdicts back to the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡上疑獄，詳覆之而無疑狀，官吏並同違制之坐。

translations.literal: Whenever doubtful cases were submitted, if after detailed review no doubtful circumstances were found, the officials were all charged equally with violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When doubtful cases were submitted, if detailed review found no grounds for doubt, the officials involved were all charged equally with violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 其應奏疑案，亦騎置以聞。

translations.literal: Doubtful cases requiring imperial submission were also reported by courier relay.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful cases requiring imperial submission were also reported by courier relay.

sentences.zh: 二年，令竊盜滿十貫者，奏裁；

translations.literal: In the second year, an order was issued that theft amounting to ten strings required submission for imperial decision;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, theft of ten strings or more required submission for imperial approval;

sentences.zh: 七貫，決杖、黥面、隸牢城；

translations.literal: Seven strings, beating, facial tattooing, and assignment to the penal colony;
translations.idiomatic: Seven strings brought beating, facial tattooing, and assignment to the penal colony;

sentences.zh: 五貫，配役三年；

translations.literal: Five strings, three years of assigned labor service;
translations.idiomatic: Five strings, three years of assigned labor;

sentences.zh: 三貫，二年；

translations.literal: Three strings, two years;
translations.idiomatic: Three strings, two years;

sentences.zh: 一貫，一年。

translations.literal: One string, one year.
translations.idiomatic: One string, one year.

sentences.zh: 它如舊制。

translations.literal: Other matters followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Other provisions followed the old system.

sentences.zh: 八月，復分遣使臣按巡諸道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, envoys were again dispatched separately to inspect the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, envoys were again dispatched to inspect the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕於獄犴之寄，夙夜焦勞，慮有滯耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the charge of the prisons, I am anxious day and night, fearing only that cases may stagnate."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In my charge over the prisons, I am anxious day and night, fearing only that cases may stagnate."

sentences.zh: 十月，親錄京城繫囚，遂至日旰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he personally reviewed the prisoners detained in the capital, continuing until the sun was setting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he personally reviewed the capital's detainees, continuing until sundown.

sentences.zh: 近臣或諫勞苦過甚，帝曰：「儻惠及無告，使獄訟平允，不致枉橈，朕意深以為適，何勞之有？」

translations.literal: Close attendants sometimes remonstrated that the labor was excessive; the emperor said: "If I can extend benefit to those with no one to plead for them, make lawsuits fair and even, and prevent wrongful distortion, my heart is deeply satisfied—what labor is there in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Close attendants sometimes urged that the effort was excessive; the emperor replied: "If I can help those with no one to plead for them, make lawsuits fair, and prevent wrongful distortion, my heart is deeply satisfied—what effort is that?"

sentences.zh: 因謂宰相曰：「中外臣僚，若皆留心政務，天下安有不治者。

translations.literal: He then said to the chief ministers: "If officials inside and outside the court all attend to governance, how could the realm fail to be well governed?
translations.idiomatic: He then told the chief ministers: "If officials throughout the court and realm all attend to governance, how could the realm fail to prosper?

sentences.zh: 古人宰一邑，守一郡，使飛蝗避境，猛虎渡河。

translations.literal: The ancients who governed one district or held one commandery could make locusts avoid their borders and tigers cross rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who governed a single district or held a single commandery could make locusts avoid their borders and tigers cross rivers unharmed.

sentences.zh: 況能惠養黎庶，申理滯，豈不感召和氣乎？

translations.literal: How much more, if one can nurture the common people with kindness and clear up delays—would this not summon harmonious qi?
translations.idiomatic: How much more, if one can nurture the people with kindness and clear up delays—would that not summon harmonious fortune?

sentences.zh: 朕每自勤不怠，此志必無改易。

translations.literal: I constantly exert myself without slackening; this resolve shall never change.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly exert myself without slackening; this resolve shall never change.

sentences.zh: 或云有司細故，帝王不當親決，朕意則異乎是。

translations.literal: Some say that minor matters of the offices are not for the emperor to decide in person; my view differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: Some say minor administrative matters are not for the emperor to decide in person; my view differs.

sentences.zh: 若以尊極自居，則下情不能上達矣。」

translations.literal: If one holds oneself aloof in supreme dignity, then the sentiments of those below cannot reach those above."
translations.idiomatic: If one holds oneself aloof in supreme dignity, the concerns of those below cannot reach the throne."

sentences.zh: 自是祁寒盛暑或雨雪稍愆，輒親錄繫囚，多所原減。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever there was severe cold, intense heat, or slight irregularity in rain and snow, he personally reviewed the detained and often granted pardons and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever severe cold, intense heat, or slight irregularity in rain and snow occurred, he personally reviewed detainees and often granted pardons and reductions.

sentences.zh: 諸道則遣官按決，率以為常，後世遵行不廢，見各帝《紀》。

translations.literal: For the various circuits, officials were dispatched to investigate and decide cases; this became the established practice, and later generations followed it without abolishing it—see each emperor's Basic Annals.
translations.idiomatic: In the circuits, officials were sent to investigate and decide cases; the practice became routine and was never abandoned by later generations—see each emperor's Basic Annals.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祝刁衎上疏言：「古者投姦人於四裔，今乃遠方囚人，盡歸象闕，配務役。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Invocator Diao Yan memorialized: "In antiquity, debauched criminals were cast out to the four borderlands; now prisoners from distant regions are all sent back to the imperial capital and assigned to corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Grand Invocator Diao Yan submitted a memorial: "In antiquity, debauched criminals were banished to the four borderlands; now prisoners from distant regions are all brought to the imperial capital and assigned to corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 神京天子所居，豈可使流囚於此聚役。

translations.literal: The divine capital is where the Son of Heaven dwells—how can exiled convicts be gathered here for labor?
translations.idiomatic: The sacred capital is the Son of Heaven's residence—how can we gather exiled convicts here for forced labor?

sentences.zh: 禮曰：『 刑 人于市，與眾棄之。』

translations.literal: The Rites say: 'Punish criminals in the market and abandon them with the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: 'Execute criminals in the marketplace and cast them out before the people.'

sentences.zh: 則知黃屋紫宸之中，非行法用刑之所。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that within the yellow-roofed palace and the purple Forbidden City is not the place to enforce law and apply punishment.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that within the imperial palace and the Forbidden City is no place to enforce the law or carry out punishments.

sentences.zh: 望自今外處罪人，勿許解送上京，亦不留於諸務充役。

translations.literal: I hope that from now on criminals from outside the capital will not be permitted to be escorted and sent up to the capital, nor retained at the various government offices to serve as laborers.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on criminals from outside the capital not be escorted to the capital, nor kept at government offices to serve as laborers.

sentences.zh: 御前不行決罰之刑 ，殿前引見司鉗黥法具、敕杖，皆以付御史、廷尉、京府。

translations.literal: Capital punishment shall not be carried out before the emperor; the shackling irons, branding implements, and imperial staffs of the Palace Reception Office should all be entrusted to the censorate, the tribunal, and the capital prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment must not be carried out in the emperor's presence; the shackles, branding tools, and imperial cudgels of the Palace Reception Office should all be entrusted to the censorate, the tribunal, and the capital prefectures.

sentences.zh: 或出中使，或命法官，具禮監科，以重明刑謹法之意。」
