translations.literal: Whether dispatching palace emissaries or appointing judicial officials, conduct the punishment with full ritual and supervision, to emphasize clarity in punishment and rigor in law."
translations.idiomatic: Whether by dispatching palace emissaries or appointing judicial officers, punishments should be carried out with full ceremony and oversight, to underscore the intent to clarify punishments and uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 帝覽疏甚悅，降詔褒答，然不能從也。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial with great satisfaction and issued an edict praising and responding to it, yet could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with great pleasure and issued an edict commending and answering it, but could not adopt his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 三年，始用儒士為司理判官，令諸州訊囚，不須眾官共視，申長吏得判乃訊囚。

translations.literal: In the third year, Confucian scholars were first employed as judicial assessors; the various prefectures were ordered that in interrogating prisoners, it was not necessary for many officials to observe together—a report to the chief official and obtaining his approval were required before interrogating prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Confucian scholars were first appointed as judicial assessors; prefectures were told that in interrogating prisoners, many officials need not observe together—instead, the chief official had to be notified and give approval before interrogation could proceed.

sentences.zh: 刑部張佖言：「官吏枉斷死罪者，請稍峻條章，以責其明慎。」

translations.literal: Zhang Bi of the Ministry of Justice said: "For officials who wrongly condemn to death, I request that the regulations be somewhat tightened to hold them accountable for clarity and caution."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi of the Ministry of Justice said: "When officials wrongly impose the death penalty, I ask that the regulations be tightened somewhat to hold them to a standard of clarity and care."

sentences.zh: 始定制：應斷獄失入死刑者，不得以官減贖，檢法官、判官皆削一任，而檢法仍贖銅十斤，長吏則停任。

translations.literal: Regulations were first established: those who in adjudicating cases wrongly imposed the death penalty could not use official rank to reduce punishment through commutation; legal examiners and assessors all had one tenure stripped, and legal examiners still had to redeem with ten jin of copper, while chief officials were suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were then established: officials who wrongly imposed the death penalty in adjudicating cases could not commute punishment by rank; legal examiners and assessors each lost one tenure, examiners still paid a ten-jin copper fine, and chief officials were suspended.

sentences.zh: 尋置刑部詳覆官六員，專閱天下所上案牘，勿復遣鞫獄吏。

translations.literal: Soon six detailed review officials of the Ministry of Justice were established, exclusively to examine case documents submitted from throughout the realm, and judicial interrogation officers were no longer dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Six Ministry of Justice review officials were soon established to examine case documents submitted from across the realm, and judicial interrogation officers were no longer dispatched.

sentences.zh: 置御史臺推勘官二十人，皆以京朝官為之。

translations.literal: Twenty investigation officers of the Censorate were established, all appointed from capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty Censorate investigation officers were established, all drawn from capital officials.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州有大獄，則乘傳就鞫。

translations.literal: Whenever any prefecture had a major case, they traveled by express relay to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prefecture had a major case, they traveled by express relay to investigate it.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，帝必臨遣諭之曰：「無滋蔓，無留滯。」

translations.literal: On the day of audience before departure, the emperor always personally attended to send them off and instructed: "Do not let cases spread; do not let them linger."
translations.idiomatic: On the day they took leave at court, the emperor always came in person to send them off and instructed: "Do not let cases proliferate; do not let them drag on."

sentences.zh: 咸賜以裝錢。

translations.literal: All were given travel money.
translations.idiomatic: All were granted travel funds.

sentences.zh: 還，必召問所推事狀，著為定令。

translations.literal: Upon return, the emperor invariably summoned them to inquire about the matters they had investigated and established this as a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, the emperor always summoned them to question them about the cases they had investigated, and this was established as a fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 自是，大理寺杖罪以下，須刑部詳覆。

translations.literal: From this time, for cases below flogging offenses at the Court of Judicial Review, Ministry of Justice detailed review was required.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all Court of Judicial Review cases below flogging required Ministry of Justice review.

sentences.zh: 又所駁天下案牘未具者，亦令詳覆乃奏。

translations.literal: Also, for case documents from throughout the realm that had been rejected as incomplete, detailed review was likewise required before memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Rejected case documents from across the realm that were incomplete likewise had to undergo review before being memorialized.

sentences.zh: 判刑部李昌齡言：「舊制，大理定刑送部，詳覆官入法狀，主判官下斷語，乃具奏。

translations.literal: Li Changling of the Ministry of Justice said: "Under the old system, when the Court of Judicial Review fixed punishment and sent cases to the ministry, the detailed review official entered the legal analysis, the chief assessor issued the decision, and only then was the memorial submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changling of the Ministry of Justice said: "Under the old system, when the Court of Judicial Review fixed a sentence and forwarded the case, the review official entered the legal analysis, the chief assessor rendered the decision, and only then was the memorial submitted.

sentences.zh: 至開寶六年，闕法直官，致兩司共斷定覆詞。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Kaibao, because the direct legal officer was vacant, both offices jointly determined the review wording.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year of Kaibao, with no direct legal officer in place, both offices jointly drafted the review language.

sentences.zh: 今宜令大理所斷案牘，寺官印署送詳覆。

translations.literal: Now it is appropriate to require that case documents adjudicated by the Court of Judicial Review be stamped and signed by court officials before sending for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: It is now appropriate to require that cases adjudicated by the Court of Judicial Review be stamped and signed by court officials before being sent for review.

sentences.zh: 得當，則送寺共奏，否即疏駁以聞。」

translations.literal: If correct, send to the court for joint memorialization; if not, submit a detailed rejection memorial."
translations.idiomatic: If correct, forward them to the court for joint memorialization; if not, submit a detailed rejection memorial."

sentences.zh: 淳化初，始置諸路提點刑獄司，凡管內州府十日一報囚帳，有疑獄未決，即馳傳往視之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, circuit offices for supervising prisons were first established in all circuits; within their jurisdictions, prefectures and commanderies reported prisoner registers every ten days, and when doubtful cases remained undecided, officials immediately traveled by express relay to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chunhua era, circuit prison-supervision offices were first established; prefectures and commanderies within each jurisdiction reported prisoner registers every ten days, and when doubtful cases remained unresolved, officials rode express relay to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 州縣稽留不決，按讞不實，長吏則劾奏，佐史、小吏許便宜按劾從事。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties delayed without deciding, or investigations did not accord with the facts, chief officials were impeached and memorialized; assistant clerks and petty officers were permitted to impeach as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectures and counties delayed decisions or investigations did not match the facts, chief officials were impeached; assistant clerks and petty officers were permitted to impeach as circumstances warranted.

sentences.zh: 帝又慮大理、刑部吏舞文巧詆，置審刑院於禁中，以樞密直學士李昌齡知院事，兼置詳議官六員。

translations.literal: The emperor also feared that clerks of the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice manipulated documents and craftily indicted; he established the Office for Review of Punishments within the palace precincts, with Privy Council academician Li Changling as director, and also established six detailed deliberation officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also feared that Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice clerks twisted documents and brought crafty indictments; he established the Office for Review of Punishments within the palace, with Privy Council academician Li Changling as director, and six deliberation officials besides.

sentences.zh: 凡獄上奏，先達審刑院，印訖，付大理寺、刑部斷覆以聞。

translations.literal: All cases submitted for memorialization first reached the Office for Review of Punishments; after stamping, they were sent to the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice for adjudication and review and reported.
translations.idiomatic: All cases submitted for memorialization first went to the Office for Review of Punishments; after stamping, they were sent to the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice for adjudication and review before being reported.

sentences.zh: 乃下審刑院詳議申覆，裁決訖，以付中書省。

translations.literal: Then they were sent down to the Office for Review of Punishments for detailed deliberation and re-review; after the decision was made, cases were forwarded to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: They were then sent to the Office for Review of Punishments for deliberation and re-review; once a decision was reached, the cases went to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 當，即下之；

translations.literal: If correct, they were immediately sent down;
translations.idiomatic: If approved, they were immediately sent down;

sentences.zh: 其未允者，宰相覆以聞，始命論決。

translations.literal: Those not approved were re-reported by the chief ministers, and only then was execution ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Those not approved were reported again by the chief ministers, and only then was execution ordered.

sentences.zh: 蓋重慎之至也。

translations.literal: This showed the utmost caution.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree of caution applied.

sentences.zh: 凡大理寺決天下案牘，大事限二十五日，中事二十日，小事十日。

translations.literal: For the Court of Judicial Review's adjudication of case documents from throughout the realm, major cases had a limit of twenty-five days, medium cases twenty days, and minor cases ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review's time limits for adjudicating cases from across the realm were twenty-five days for major cases, twenty for medium cases, and ten for minor ones.

sentences.zh: 審刑院詳覆，大事十五日，中事十日，小事五日。

translations.literal: For the Office for Review of Punishments' detailed review, major cases fifteen days, medium cases ten days, and minor cases five days.
translations.idiomatic: The Office for Review of Punishments allowed fifteen days for major cases, ten for medium cases, and five for minor ones.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔御史臺鞫徒以上罪，獄具，令尚書丞郎、兩省給舍以上一人親往慮問。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered that when the Censorate interrogated offenses of penal servitude and above and the case was complete, one Vice Minister or Director of a ministry, or one drafter of edicts from the two secretariats or above, should personally go to examine and question the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict ordered that when the Censorate finished interrogating offenses of penal servitude or above, one Vice Minister, Director, or drafter of edicts from the two secretariats or higher had to go in person to examine and question the prisoner.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔：「獄無大小，自中丞以下，皆臨鞫問，不得專責所司。」

translations.literal: Soon another edict stated: "Cases large and small—from the Vice Censor-in-Chief down, all must personally conduct interrogation and may not solely delegate to the responsible office."
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict stated: "Cases great and small—from the Vice Censor-in-Chief down, all must personally conduct interrogations and may not leave the matter solely to the responsible office."

sentences.zh: 自端拱以來，諸州司理參軍，皆帝自選擇，民有詣闕稱者，亦遣臺使乘傳按鞫，數年之間，刑罰清省矣。

translations.literal: From the Duan Gong era onward, judicial military officers of the various prefectures were all personally selected by the emperor; when commoners came to the palace to lodge petitions, envoys of the Censorate were also dispatched by express relay to investigate and interrogate; within a few years, punishments were clear and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: From the Duan Gong era on, judicial officers in the prefectures were all personally chosen by the emperor; when commoners came to court to petition, Censorate envoys were also sent by express relay to investigate; within a few years, punishments became clearer and lighter.

sentences.zh: 既而諸路提點刑獄司未嘗有所平反，詔悉罷之，歸其事轉運司。

translations.literal: Before long, since the circuit prison-supervision offices had never reversed any cases, an edict abolished them all and returned their duties to the transport commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because the circuit prison-supervision offices had never overturned a single case, an edict abolished them all and returned their duties to the transport commissions.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，帝聞諸州所斷大辟，情可疑者，懼為有司所駁，不敢上其獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, the emperor heard that among capital cases decided by the various prefectures, where the circumstances were doubtful, officials feared rejection by the responsible offices and did not dare submit their cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao, the emperor learned that when prefectures decided capital cases with doubtful circumstances, officials feared rejection by higher offices and did not dare submit them.

sentences.zh: 迺詔死事有可疑者，具獄申轉運司，擇部內詳練格律者令決之，須奏者乃奏。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: when death cases were doubtful, submit the complete case to the transport commission; select someone within the commission thoroughly versed in statutes and regulations to decide it—only those requiring memorialization were to be memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: doubtful death cases were to be submitted in full to the transport commission, which would choose someone well versed in statutes to decide them—only cases requiring memorialization were to be memorialized.

sentences.zh: 真宗性寬慈，尤慎刑辟。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong was by nature lenient and compassionate, and especially cautious in capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was by nature lenient and compassionate, and especially cautious in applying capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂宰相曰：「執法之吏，不可輕授。

translations.literal: He once told the chief ministers: "Officers who enforce the law must not be lightly appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He once told the chief ministers: "Officers who enforce the law must not be appointed lightly.

sentences.zh: 有不稱職者，當責舉主，以懲其濫。」

translations.literal: When any prove unfit for office, the recommender should be held accountable to punish indiscriminate recommendation."
translations.idiomatic: When any prove unfit, the recommender should be held accountable, to punish careless nomination."

sentences.zh: 審刑院舉詳議官，就刑部試斷案三十二道，取引用詳明者。

translations.literal: The Office for Review of Punishments recommended detailed deliberation officials by testing them at the Ministry of Justice on thirty-two sample cases, selecting those whose citations were thorough and clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Office for Review of Punishments selected deliberation officials by testing them at the Ministry of Justice on thirty-two sample cases, choosing those whose legal citations were thorough and clear.

sentences.zh: 審刑院每奏案，令先具事狀，親覽之，翌日，乃候進止，裁處輕重，必當其罪。

translations.literal: Whenever the Office for Review of Punishments memorialized a case, the emperor ordered that the facts first be fully presented; he personally read them, and the next day awaited his decision; in determining severity, the punishment must fit the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Office for Review of Punishments memorialized a case, the facts were first fully presented for the emperor's personal review; the next day he awaited his decision, and in fixing severity the punishment had to fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，從黃州守王禹偁之請，諸路置病囚院，徒、流以上有疾者處之，餘責保于外。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, following the request of Wang Yucheng, prefect of Huangzhou, sick-prisoner wards were established in all circuits; those sentenced to penal servitude, exile, or above who were ill were housed there, while others were held on bail outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping, at the request of Huangzhou prefect Wang Yucheng, sick-prisoner wards were established in all circuits; convicts sentenced to penal servitude, exile, or above who fell ill were housed there, while others were released on bail.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，詔：「諸道州軍斷獄，內有宣敕不定刑名，止言當行極斷者，所在即寘大辟，頗乖平允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, an edict stated: "When prefectures and armies in the various circuits adjudicate cases, some imperial orders do not specify the name of the punishment but only say 'shall be executed to the utmost'—local offices immediately impose capital punishment, which greatly deviates from fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde, an edict stated: "When prefectures and military commands adjudicate cases, some imperial orders do not specify the punishment but only say 'shall be executed to the utmost'—local offices immediately impose death, which greatly violates fairness.

sentences.zh: 自今凡言處斷、重斷、極斷、決配、朝典之類，未得論決，具獄以聞。」

translations.literal: From now on, for any terms such as execution, heavy execution, utmost execution, exile by decree, or court punishment—without deciding by themselves, submit the complete case for imperial review."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for any order using terms such as execution, heavy execution, utmost execution, exile by decree, or court punishment, local offices may not decide on their own but must submit the complete case for imperial review."

sentences.zh: 四年，復置諸路提點刑獄官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, circuit prison-supervision officials were reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, circuit prison-supervision officials were reestablished.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝出筆記六事，其一曰：「勤恤民隱，遴柬庶官，朕無日不念也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor issued a written note on six matters; the first said: "Diligently caring for the people's hidden grievances and carefully selecting officials—I think of this without fail every day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor issued a written note on six matters; the first read: "Diligently tending the people's hidden grievances and carefully selecting officials—I think of this every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 所慮四方刑獄官吏，未盡得人，一夫受，即召災沴。

translations.literal: What I fear is that prison officials throughout the realm are not all the right men; when one person suffers wrongful punishment, calamity is immediately summoned.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear is that prison officials throughout the realm are not all fit for their posts; when one person suffers injustice, calamity is summoned at once.

sentences.zh: 今軍民事務，雖有轉運使，且地遠無由周知。

translations.literal: Now for military and civilian affairs, although there are transport commissioners, the distance is great and there is no way to know everything.
translations.idiomatic: For military and civilian affairs today, although transport commissioners exist, the distances are great and there is no way to know everything.

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗選朝臣為諸路提點刑獄，今可復置，仍以使臣副之，命中書、樞密院擇官。」

translations.literal: The previous emperor once selected court officials as circuit prison supervisors; now they may be reestablished, with envoy-officials as deputies, ordering the Secretariat and Privy Council to choose the officials."
translations.idiomatic: The previous emperor once selected court officials as circuit prison supervisors; they may now be reestablished, with envoy-officials as deputies, and the Secretariat and Privy Council ordered to choose the men."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「河北、陝西，地控邊要，尤必得人，須性度平和有執守者。」

translations.literal: Another item said: "Hebei and Shaanxi, controlling crucial border regions, especially require the right men—those of even temperament and steadfast principle."
translations.idiomatic: Another item read: "Hebei and Shaanxi, guarding critical border regions, especially require the right men—men of even temperament and steadfast principle."

sentences.zh: 親選太常博士陳綱、李及，自餘擬名以聞，咸引對於長春殿遣之。

translations.literal: He personally selected Grand Masters of Ceremonies Chen Gang and Li Ji; for the rest, proposed names were reported; all were summoned to audience at the Changchun Hall and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: He personally selected Grand Masters of Ceremonies Chen Gang and Li Ji; for the rest, proposed names were reported; all were granted audience at the Changchun Hall and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 內出御前印紙為曆，書其績效，代還，議功行賞。

translations.literal: From within the palace, sealed papers bearing the imperial seal were issued as record books to note their achievements; upon return, merit was assessed and rewards granted.
translations.idiomatic: The palace issued sealed record books bearing the imperial seal to track their performance; on their return, merit was assessed and rewards granted.

sentences.zh: 如刑獄枉濫不能擿舉，官吏曠不能彈奏，務從畏避者，寘以深罪。

translations.literal: If they could not expose wrongful abuse in prisons, or could not impeach negligent officials, and deliberately practiced evasion, they were punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: If they failed to expose wrongful abuse in prisons or impeach negligent officials, and deliberately shrank from their duties, they were punished severely.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院朱巽上言：「官吏因公事受財，證左明白，望論以枉法，其罪至死者，加役流。」

translations.literal: Zhu Xun, director of the Office for Review of Punishments, submitted: "When officials accept bribes in public affairs with clear evidence, I hope they may be judged as perverting the law; those whose crime reaches death should receive penal servitude in addition."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xun, director of the Office for Review of Punishments, submitted: "When officials accept bribes in the course of public business with clear evidence, I ask that they be judged for perverting the law; those whose crime would otherwise merit death should receive penal servitude instead."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 御史臺嘗鞫殺人賊，獄具，知雜王隨請臠咼之，帝曰：「五刑自有常制，何為慘毒也。」

translations.literal: The Censorate once interrogated a murderer; when the case was complete, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sui requested that he be dismembered and mutilated; the emperor said: "The five punishments have their fixed regulations—why be cruel and savage?"
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate once interrogated a murderer; when the case was complete, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sui asked that he be dismembered; the emperor said: "The five punishments have their fixed standards—why resort to such cruelty?"

sentences.zh: 入內供奉官楊守珍使陝西，督捕盜賊，因請「擒獲強盜至死者，望以付臣凌遲，用戒凶惡」。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yang Shouzhen was sent to Shaanxi to supervise the capture of bandits, and requested: "For captured robbers whose crime reaches death, I hope they may be handed over to me for lingchi execution, to warn the vicious and wicked."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yang Shouzhen was sent to Shaanxi to supervise the capture of bandits and requested: "For captured robbers whose crime merits death, I ask that they be handed over to me for lingchi execution, to warn the vicious and wicked."

sentences.zh: 詔：「捕賊送所屬，依法論決，毋用凌遲。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Captured bandits shall be sent to the responsible jurisdiction and judged according to law—do not use lingchi."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Captured bandits shall be sent to the responsible jurisdiction and judged according to law—do not use lingchi."

sentences.zh: 凌遲者，先斷其支體，乃抉其吭，當時之極法也。

translations.literal: Lingchi meant first cutting off the limbs, then severing the throat—it was the extreme punishment of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchi meant first cutting off the limbs, then severing the throat—it was the most extreme punishment of the age.

sentences.zh: 蓋真宗仁恕，而慘酷之刑 ，祖宗亦未嘗用。

translations.literal: For Zhenzong was benevolent and forgiving, and even cruel punishments—the imperial ancestors had never used them either.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhenzong was benevolent and forgiving, and even cruel punishments—the imperial ancestors had never employed them.

sentences.zh: 初，殿中侍御史趙湘嘗建言：「聖王行法，必順天道。

translations.literal: Initially, Palace Censor Zhao Xiang once submitted a proposal: "A sage king enforces law by necessarily conforming to the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Censor Zhao Xiang once submitted a proposal: "A sage king enforces the law in accord with the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 漢制大辟之科，盡冬月乃斷。

translations.literal: Under Han law, capital offenses were all executed only in winter months.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, capital offenses were executed only during the winter months.

sentences.zh: 此古之善政，當舉行之。

translations.literal: This was fine governance of antiquity and ought to be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: This was sound governance of antiquity and ought to be revived.

sentences.zh: 且十二月為承天節，萬方祝頌之時，而大辟決斷如故。

translations.literal: Moreover, the twelfth month is the Chengtian Festival, when all regions offer blessings—yet capital executions proceed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the twelfth month is the Chengtian Festival, when all regions offer blessings—yet capital executions continue as before.

sentences.zh: 况十一月一陽始出，其氣尚微，議獄緩刑 ，所以助陽抑陰也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the eleventh month the single yang first emerges and its qi is still weak; deliberating cases and deferring punishments serve to assist yang and suppress yin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the eleventh month the single yang first emerges and its qi is still weak; deliberating cases and deferring punishments help yang rise and yin recede.

sentences.zh: 望以十一月、十二月內，天下大辟未結正者，更令詳覆；

translations.literal: I hope that within the eleventh and twelfth months, all capital cases throughout the realm not yet finalized shall be ordered for renewed detailed review;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that during the eleventh and twelfth months, all capital cases throughout the realm not yet finalized be ordered for renewed review;

sentences.zh: 已結正者，未令決斷。

translations.literal: Those already finalized shall not be ordered executed.
translations.idiomatic: Those already finalized shall not be executed.

sentences.zh: 所在厚加矜恤，掃除獄房，供給飲食、薪炭之屬，防護無致他故。

translations.literal: Everywhere they should be treated with extra compassion, prison cells cleaned, food, drink, firewood, and charcoal supplied, and guarded so that no other mishap occurs.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere they should receive extra compassion: prison cells cleaned, food, drink, firewood, and charcoal supplied, and guards posted so that no other mishap befalls them.

sentences.zh: 情可憫者，奏聽敕裁。

translations.literal: Those whose circumstances merit pity should be memorialized for the emperor's merciful decision.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose circumstances merit pity should be memorialized for the emperor's merciful judgment.

sentences.zh: 合依法者，盡冬月乃斷。

translations.literal: Those who must be punished according to law should be executed only when the winter months are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Those who must be punished according to law should be executed only after the winter months have passed.

sentences.zh: 在京大辟人，既當春孟之月，亦行慶施惠之時。

translations.literal: For capital convicts in the capital, since it is now the first month of spring, it is also a time for celebration and granting favors.
translations.idiomatic: For capital convicts in the capital, since it is now early spring, it is also a time for celebration and the granting of favors.

sentences.zh: 伏望萬幾之暇，臨軒躬覽，情可憫者，特從末減，亦所以布聖澤於無窮。

translations.literal: I humbly hope that in the leisure from myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty may personally review them at the throne; for those whose circumstances merit pity, grant special leniency—thus spreading imperial grace without limit.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope that amid the myriad affairs of state, Your Majesty will personally review them from the throne; for those whose circumstances merit pity, grant special leniency—thus spreading imperial grace without end.

sentences.zh: 况愚民之抵罪未斷，兩月亦非淹延。

translations.literal: Moreover, for common people awaiting judgment on their offenses, two months would not constitute delay.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for common people awaiting judgment, two months would hardly count as delay.

sentences.zh: 若用刑順於陰陽，則四時之氣和，氣和則百穀豐實，水旱不作矣。」

translations.literal: If punishments accord with yin and yang, then the qi of the four seasons will harmonize; when qi harmonizes, the hundred grains will flourish and drought and flood will not occur."
translations.idiomatic: If punishments accord with yin and yang, the qi of the four seasons will harmonize; when qi harmonizes, the hundred grains flourish and drought and flood do not occur."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏曰：「此誠嘉事！

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and said: "This is truly a worthy proposal!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and said: "This is truly a worthy proposal!

sentences.zh: 然古今異制，沿革不同，行之慮有淹滯，或因緣為姦矣。」

translations.literal: Yet ancient and modern systems differ and institutions have evolved—if implemented, I fear there may be delay, or opportunities for corruption."
translations.idiomatic: Yet ancient and modern systems differ and institutions have evolved—if implemented, I fear there may be delay, or opportunities for abuse."

sentences.zh: 天禧四年乃詔：「天下犯十惡、劫殺、謀殺、故殺、鬥殺、放火、強劫、正枉法贓、偽造符印、厭魅咒詛、造妖書妖言、傳授妖術、合造毒藥、禁軍諸軍逃亡為盜罪至死者，每遇十二月，權住區斷，過天慶節即決之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, an edict was issued: "For crimes throughout the realm of the ten abominations, robbery-murder, plotted murder, intentional murder, brawling murder, arson, armed robbery, outright perversion of law for bribes, forging seals and credentials, sorcery and cursing, creating seditious writings and words, teaching occult arts, compounding poisons, and desertion from the forbidden armies or other armies to become bandits—all where the crime reaches death—whenever the twelfth month arrives, execution shall be temporarily suspended; after the Tianqing Festival, they shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi, an edict was issued: "For crimes throughout the realm—the ten abominations, robbery-murder, plotted murder, intentional murder, brawling murder, arson, armed robbery, outright perversion of law for bribes, forging seals and credentials, sorcery and cursing, creating seditious writings and words, teaching occult arts, compounding poisons, and desertion from the forbidden armies or other armies to become bandits—wherever the crime merits death, whenever the twelfth month arrives, execution shall be temporarily suspended; after the Tianqing Festival, they shall be executed.

sentences.zh: 餘犯至死者，十二月及春夏未得區遣，禁錮奏裁。」

translations.literal: For other offenses reaching death, during the twelfth month and spring and summer they may not be executed; they shall be imprisoned pending memorialized decision."
translations.idiomatic: For other capital offenses, during the twelfth month and spring and summer they may not be executed; they shall be imprisoned pending memorialized decision."

sentences.zh: 在仁宗時，四方無事，戶口蕃息，而克自抑畏，其於用刑尤慎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Renzong's reign, the four quarters were at peace, the population flourished, and he restrained himself with humility; in applying punishment he was especially cautious.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Renzong's reign, the realm was at peace on all sides, the population flourished, and he restrained himself with humility; in applying punishment he was especially cautious.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，詔內外官司，聽獄決罪，須躬自閱實，毋枉濫淹滯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his reign, an edict ordered internal and external offices that in hearing cases and deciding guilt, they must personally verify the facts, without wrongful abuse or protracted delay.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his reign, an edict ordered all offices, internal and external, that in hearing cases and deciding guilt they must personally verify the facts, without wrongful abuse or protracted delay.

sentences.zh: 刑部嘗薦詳覆官，帝記其姓名，曰：「是嘗失入人罪不得遷官者，烏可任法吏？」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice once recommended detailed review officials; the emperor remembered their names and said: "These are ones who wrongly imposed guilt on others and were barred from promotion—how can they serve as legal officers?"
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice once recommended review officials; the emperor remembered their names and said: "These are the ones who wrongly convicted others and were barred from promotion—how can they serve as legal officers?"

sentences.zh: 舉者皆罰金。

translations.literal: Those who recommended them all were fined.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had recommended them were all fined.

sentences.zh: 獄疑者讞，所從來久矣。

translations.literal: The practice of deliberating on doubtful cases has existed from long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation on doubtful cases is an ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 漢嘗詔「讞而後不當讞者不為失」，所以廣聽察、防繆濫也。

translations.literal: Han once decreed that "if after deliberation the deliberation proves wrong, it is not counted as error"—thereby broadening scrutiny and preventing wrongful abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Han once decreed that "if after deliberation the deliberation proves wrong, it is not counted as error"—thereby broadening scrutiny and preventing abuse.

sentences.zh: 時奏讞之法廢。

translations.literal: At this time the practice of memorializing for deliberation had been abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the practice of memorializing for deliberation had been abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗嘗覽囚簿，見天下斷死罪八百人，憮然動容，語宰執曰：「雜犯死罪條目至多，官吏儻不盡心，豈無枉濫？

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Zhenzong once reviewed the prisoner register, saw eight hundred death sentences throughout the realm, and was visibly moved; he told the chief ministers: "There are so many categories of miscellaneous capital crimes—if officials do not exert themselves fully, could there not be wrongful abuse?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Zhenzong once reviewed the prisoner register, saw eight hundred death sentences throughout the realm, and was visibly moved; he told the chief ministers: "There are so many categories of capital crimes—if officials do not exert themselves fully, could there not be wrongful convictions?

sentences.zh: 故事，死罪獄具，三覆奏，蓋甚重慎，何代罷之？」

translations.literal: Former precedent required that when capital cases were complete, there be three review memorializations—showing great caution—in which reign was this abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: Former precedent required three review memorializations when capital cases were complete—showing great caution—in which reign was this abolished?"

sentences.zh: 遂命檢討革，而有司終慮淹繫，不果行。

translations.literal: An order was issued to investigate and restore it, but the responsible offices ultimately feared prolonged detention and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an investigation to restore the practice, but the responsible offices ultimately feared prolonged detention and it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 至是，刑部侍郎燕肅奏曰：「唐大辟罪，令尚書、九卿讞之。

translations.literal: At this time, Vice Minister of Justice Yan Su memorialized: "Under Tang, for capital crimes, Ministers and the Nine Ministers were ordered to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Vice Minister of Justice Yan Su memorialized: "Under Tang, capital crimes were referred to the Ministers and the Nine Ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 凡決死刑，京師五覆奏，諸州三覆奏。

translations.literal: For all death sentences, in the capital there were five review memorializations, in the prefectures three.
translations.idiomatic: For all death sentences, the capital required five review memorializations and the prefectures three.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，斷死罪二十九，開元二十五年，財五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, twenty-nine death sentences; in the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, only fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, there were twenty-nine death sentences; in the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, only fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 今天下生齒未加於唐，而天聖三年，斷大辟二千四百三十六，視唐幾至百倍。

translations.literal: Today the population has not exceeded that of Tang, yet in the third year of Tiansheng, capital sentences numbered 2,436—nearly a hundred times Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Today the population has not surpassed Tang's, yet in the third year of Tiansheng there were 2,436 capital sentences—nearly a hundred times Tang's numbers.

sentences.zh: 京師大辟雖一覆奏，而州郡獄疑上請，法寺多所舉駁，率得不應奏之罪，往往增飾事狀，移情就法，失朝廷欽恤之意。

translations.literal: Although in the capital there was one review memorialization for capital cases, when prefectures submitted doubtful cases for imperial review, the judicial courts often rejected them, usually resulting in non-reportable offenses; officials often embellished the facts and shifted circumstances to fit the law, losing the court's intent of merciful consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Although the capital required one review memorialization for capital cases, when prefectures submitted doubtful cases for imperial review, the judicial courts often rejected them, usually yielding non-reportable offenses; officials often embellished the facts and shifted circumstances to fit the law, betraying the court's intent of merciful consideration.

sentences.zh: 望準唐故事，天下死罪皆得覆奏。

translations.literal: I hope that following Tang precedent, all death sentences throughout the realm may receive review memorialization.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that following Tang precedent, all death sentences throughout the realm receive review memorialization.

sentences.zh: 議者必曰待報淹延。

translations.literal: Critics will surely say that awaiting approval causes delay.
translations.idiomatic: Critics will surely say that awaiting approval causes delay.

sentences.zh: 漢律皆以季秋論囚，唐自立春至秋分不決死刑，未聞淹留以害漢、唐之治也。」

translations.literal: Han law deliberated on prisoners entirely in late autumn; Tang from the first month of spring until the autumn equinox did not execute capital punishment—yet no one has heard that such delay harmed the governance of Han and Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Han law deliberated on prisoners entirely in late autumn; Tang from early spring until the autumn equinox did not execute capital punishment—yet no one has heard that such delay harmed the governance of Han and Tang."

sentences.zh: 下其章中書，王曾謂：「天下皆一覆奏，則必死之人，徒充滿狴犴而久不得決。

translations.literal: The memorial was forwarded to the Secretariat. Wang Zeng said: "If the entire realm uniformly requires review memorialization, then those who must die will merely fill the prisons and long go without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was forwarded to the Secretariat. Wang Zeng said: "If every death sentence throughout the realm must receive review memorialization, those condemned to die will merely fill the prisons while judgment is long deferred.

sentences.zh: 諸獄疑若情可矜者，聽上請。」

translations.literal: In all prisons, if a case is doubtful or the circumstances merit pity, they were permitted to submit a memorial upward."
translations.idiomatic: In all prisons, doubtful cases or those whose circumstances merited pity were permitted to submit memorials for review."

sentences.zh: 天聖四年，遂下詔曰：「朕念生齒之蕃，抵冒者眾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, an edict was then issued stating: "We consider that the population has grown abundant and those who offend are many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, an edict was issued: "We note that the population has grown abundant and offenders are many.

sentences.zh: 法有高下，情有輕重，而有司巧避微文，一切致之重辟，豈稱朕好生之志哉？

translations.literal: The law has gradations and circumstances have degrees of severity, yet officials cleverly evade fine points of text and uniformly bring cases to capital punishment—how does this accord with Our will to cherish life?
translations.idiomatic: The law has gradations and circumstances vary in severity, yet officials cleverly evade fine points of text and uniformly impose capital punishment—how does this accord with Our will to cherish life?

sentences.zh: 其令天下死罪，情理可矜及刑名疑慮者，具案以聞。

translations.literal: Let all death sentences throughout the realm, where the circumstances merit pity or where the charge raises doubt, be fully reported in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Let all death sentences throughout the realm whose circumstances merit pity or whose charges raise doubt be fully reported in memorial.

sentences.zh: 有司毋得舉駁。」

translations.literal: Officials must not raise objections."
translations.idiomatic: Officials were forbidden to raise objections."

sentences.zh: 其後，雖法不應奏、吏當坐罪者，審刑院貼奏，率以恩釋為例，名曰「貼放」。

translations.literal: Thereafter, even when the law did not require memorialization and officials should have been punished, the Office for Review of Punishments submitted attached memorials, generally taking clemency and release as precedent—a practice called "attached release."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, even when the law did not require memorialization and officials ought to have been punished, the Office for Review of Punishments submitted attached memorials, generally treating clemency and release as precedent—a practice called "attached release."

sentences.zh: 吏始無所牽制，請讞者多得減死矣。

translations.literal: Officials were at last unrestrained, and those who memorialized for sentence review often had death sentences commuted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were at last unrestrained, and those who memorialized for sentence review often had death sentences commuted.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下旬奏獄狀，雖杖、笞皆申覆，而徒、流罪非繫獄，乃不以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, the realm submitted prison reports every ten days; even beatings with rod or stick were reported for review, yet penal servitude and exile, not being held in prison, were not reported.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, prison reports were submitted throughout the realm every ten days; even beatings with rod or stick were reported for review, yet penal servitude and exile, since the convicts were not held in prison, went unreported.

sentences.zh: 六年，集賢校理聶冠卿請罷覆杖、笞，而徒以上雖不繫獄，皆附奏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Nie Guanqing, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, requested abolishing review of rod and stick beatings, while for penal servitude and above, even when not held in prison, all cases should be attached to memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Nie Guanqing, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, requested abolishing review of rod and stick beatings and requiring that all sentences from penal servitude upward, even when the convict was not held in prison, be attached to memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔從其說。

translations.literal: An edict approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 自定折杖之制，杖之長短廣狹，皆有尺度，而輕重無準，官吏得以任情。

translations.literal: Since the system of commuted beatings was established, the length, width, and thickness of rods all had fixed measures, yet the severity had no standard, and officials could act at will.
translations.idiomatic: Since the system of commuted beatings was established, the length, width, and thickness of rods all had fixed measures, yet severity had no standard and officials could act at will.

sentences.zh: 至是，有司以為言，詔毋過十五兩。

translations.literal: At this point officials raised the matter, and an edict fixed the weight at no more than fifteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: At this point officials raised the matter, and an edict fixed the weight at no more than fifteen liang.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗時，以京師刑獄多滯，置糾察司，而御史臺獄亦移報之。

translations.literal: Initially, under Zhenzong, because criminal cases in the capital often stagnated, an Inspection Office was established, and cases in the Censorate prison were also transferred for report to it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, under Zhenzong, because criminal cases in the capital often stagnated, an Inspection Office was established, and cases in the Censorate prison were also reported to it.

sentences.zh: 八年，御史論以為非體，遂詔勿報。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, censors argued that this was improper, and an edict ordered that reports cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, censors argued that this was improper, and an edict ordered that such reports cease.

sentences.zh: 祖宗時，重盜剝桑柘之禁，枯者以尺計，積四十二尺為一功，三功以上抵死。

translations.literal: In the time of the imperial ancestors, the prohibition on stealing and stripping mulberry and ramie trees was strictly enforced; withered branches were measured by the foot, forty-two feet accumulated counted as one offense, and three offenses or more merited death.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of the imperial ancestors, the prohibition on stealing and stripping mulberry and ramie trees was strictly enforced; withered branches were measured by the foot, forty-two feet counted as one offense, and three offenses or more merited death.

sentences.zh: 殿中丞于大成請得以減死論，下法官議，謂當如舊。

translations.literal: Palace Administration Aide Yu Dacheng requested that such cases be judged with commutation from death; the matter was referred to legal officials for deliberation, who said the old rule should stand.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Administration Aide Yu Dacheng requested that such cases be judged with commutation from death; the matter was referred to legal officials for deliberation, who ruled that the old standard should stand.

sentences.zh: 帝意欲寬之，詔死者上請。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to leniently treat the matter and ordered that death sentences be submitted upward for review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to leniently treat the matter and ordered that death sentences be submitted upward for review.

sentences.zh: 刑部分四按，大辟居其一，月覆大辟不下二百數，而詳覆官纔一人。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice was divided into four review sections, capital cases occupying one section; each month capital cases reviewed numbered no less than two hundred, yet there was only one detailed review official.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice was divided into four review sections, capital cases occupying one; each month no fewer than two hundred capital cases came up for review, yet there was only one detailed review official.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，令四按分覆大辟，有能駁正死罪五人以上，歲滿改官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, the four sections were ordered to divide review of capital cases; those who could overturn five or more death sentences, upon completing their term, received promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao, the four sections were ordered to divide review of capital cases; officials who overturned five or more death sentences received promotion upon completing their term.

sentences.zh: 法直官與詳覆官分詳天下旬奏，獄有重辟，獄官毋預燕遊迎送。

translations.literal: Legal examiners and detailed review officials divided review of the realm's ten-day prison reports; when a case involved capital punishment, prison officials were not to participate in banquets, outings, or escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Legal examiners and detailed review officials divided review of the realm's ten-day prison reports; when a case involved capital punishment, prison officials were forbidden to attend banquets, outings, or escort duties.

sentences.zh: 凡上具獄，大理寺詳斷，大事期三十日，小事第減十日。

translations.literal: For all completed cases submitted upward, the Court of Judicial Review conducted detailed judgment: major cases had a deadline of thirty days, minor cases ten days less.
translations.idiomatic: For all completed cases submitted upward, the Court of Judicial Review conducted detailed judgment: major cases had a deadline of thirty days, minor cases ten days less.

sentences.zh: 審刑院詳議又各減半。

translations.literal: The Office for Review of Punishments' detailed deliberation reduced each by half again.
translations.idiomatic: The Office for Review of Punishments' detailed deliberation halved each deadline again.

sentences.zh: 其不待期滿而斷者，謂之「急按」。

translations.literal: Those decided before the deadline expired were called "expedited cases."
translations.idiomatic: Cases decided before the deadline expired were called "expedited cases."

sentences.zh: 凡集斷急按，法官與議者並書姓名，議刑有失，則皆坐之。

translations.literal: For all expedited cases decided in assembly, judges and deliberators all wrote their names; if the deliberated punishment was in error, all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: For all expedited cases decided in assembly, judges and deliberators all signed their names; if the deliberated punishment was in error, all were held accountable.

sentences.zh: 至景祐二年，判大理寺司徒昌運言：「斷獄有期日，而炎暍之時，繫囚淹久，請自四月至六月減期日之半，兩川、廣南、福建、湖南如急按奏。」

translations.literal: By the second year of Jingyou, Situ Changyun, acting director of the Court of Judicial Review, said: "Cases have fixed deadlines, yet in hot and sultry seasons prisoners are long detained; I request that from the fourth to the sixth month deadlines be halved, and in the Two Sichuans, Guangnan, Fujian, and Hunan cases be submitted like expedited cases."
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Jingyou, Situ Changyun, acting director of the Court of Judicial Review, said: "Cases have fixed deadlines, yet in hot and sultry seasons prisoners are long detained; I request that from the fourth to the sixth month deadlines be halved, and that in the Two Sichuans, Guangnan, Fujian, and Hunan cases be submitted as expedited cases."

sentences.zh: 其後猶以斷獄淹滯，又詔月上斷獄數，列大、中，小事期日，以相參考。

translations.literal: Thereafter, because cases still stagnated, an edict also required monthly reports of cases decided, listing deadlines for major, medium, and minor cases for mutual reference.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, because cases still stagnated, an edict also required monthly reports of cases decided, listing deadlines for major, medium, and minor cases for cross-reference.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改強盜法。

translations.literal: That year, the law on robbery was revised.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the law on robbery was revised.

sentences.zh: 不持杖，不得財，徒二年；

translations.literal: Without carrying a weapon, if no property was taken, penal servitude for two years;
translations.idiomatic: Without carrying a weapon, if no property was taken, penal servitude for two years;

sentences.zh: 得財為錢萬及傷人者，死。

translations.literal: if property taken amounted to ten thousand cash or a person was injured, death.
translations.idiomatic: if property taken amounted to ten thousand cash or a person was injured, death.

sentences.zh: 持杖而不得財，流三千里；

translations.literal: Carrying a weapon but taking no property, exile three thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Carrying a weapon but taking no property, exile three thousand li;

sentences.zh: 得財為錢五千者，死；

translations.literal: if property taken amounted to five thousand cash, death;
translations.idiomatic: if property taken amounted to five thousand cash, death;

sentences.zh: 傷人者，殊死。

translations.literal: if a person was injured, execution by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: if a person was injured, execution by decapitation.

sentences.zh: 不持杖得財為錢六千，若持杖罪不至死者，仍刺隸千里外牢城。

translations.literal: Without carrying a weapon, if property taken amounted to six thousand cash, or if carrying a weapon the crime did not reach death, they were still tattooed and registered as convict labor in fortress cities a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Without carrying a weapon, if property taken amounted to six thousand cash, or if carrying a weapon the crime did not merit death, the offender was still tattooed and registered as convict labor in fortress cities a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 能告?盜劫殺人者第賞之，及十人者予錢十萬。

translations.literal: Those who could report bandits acting in groups who robbed and killed were rewarded according to rank; those reaching ten men received one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Those who reported bandits acting in groups who robbed and killed were rewarded according to merit; informants whose reports covered ten or more offenders received one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 既而有司言：「竊盜不用威力，得財為錢五千，即刺為兵，反重於強盜，請減之。」

translations.literal: Soon after officials said: "Petty theft without use of force, if property taken amounted to five thousand cash, immediately resulted in tattooing as soldier—this is in fact heavier than robbery; we request reduction."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after officials said: "Petty theft without use of force, if property taken amounted to five thousand cash, immediately resulted in tattooing as soldier—heavier in fact than robbery; we request a reduction."

sentences.zh: 遂詔至十千始刺為兵，而京城持杖竊盜，得財為錢四千，亦刺為兵。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that tattooing as soldier began only at ten thousand cash, while in the capital, armed petty theft with property taken amounting to four thousand cash also resulted in tattooing as soldier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued that tattooing as soldier began only at ten thousand cash, while in the capital armed petty theft with property taken amounting to four thousand cash also resulted in tattooing as soldier.

sentences.zh: 自是盜法惟京城加重，餘視舊益寬矣。

translations.literal: From this time only the capital had heavier theft law; elsewhere the old law was viewed as increasingly lenient.
translations.idiomatic: From this time only the capital had heavier theft law; elsewhere the old standards were increasingly lenient.

sentences.zh: 慶曆五年，詔罪殊死者，若祖父母、父母年八十及篤疾無期親者，列所犯以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingli, an edict ordered that for crimes meriting execution by decapitation, if grandparents or parents were eighty years old or seriously ill with no other close kin, the offense should be listed and reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qingli, an edict ordered that for crimes meriting execution by decapitation, if grandparents or parents were eighty years old or seriously ill with no other close kin, the offense should be listed and reported.

sentences.zh: 承平日久，天下生齒益蕃，犯法者多，歲斷大辟甚眾，而有司未嘗上其數。

translations.literal: Peace had long endured; the population throughout the realm grew ever more abundant, lawbreakers were many, and capital cases decided each year were extremely numerous—yet officials had never reported the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had long endured; the population throughout the realm grew ever more abundant, lawbreakers were many, and capital cases decided each year were extremely numerous—yet officials had never reported the numbers.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐五年，判刑部李綖言：「一歲之中，死刑無慮二千餘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiayou, Li Yuan, vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, said: "Within one year, death sentences number no less than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiayou, Li Yuan, vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, said: "Within one year, death sentences number no less than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 夫風俗之薄，無甚於骨肉相殘；

translations.literal: Of the decline in custom, nothing is worse than kin slaughtering kin;
translations.idiomatic: Of the decline in custom, nothing is worse than kin slaughtering kin;

sentences.zh: 衣食之窮莫急於盜賊。

translations.literal: of the extremity of want in food and clothing, nothing is more urgent than bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: of the extremity of want in food and clothing, nothing is more urgent than bandits and thieves.

sentences.zh: 今犯法者眾，豈刑罰不足以止姦，而教化未能導其為善歟？

translations.literal: Now lawbreakers are many—is it that punishments are insufficient to stop wickedness, or that instruction and transformation have not yet guided them toward goodness?
translations.idiomatic: Now lawbreakers are many—is it that punishments are insufficient to stop wickedness, or that instruction and transformation have not yet guided them toward goodness?

sentences.zh: 願詔刑部類天下所斷大辟，歲上朝廷，以助觀省。」

translations.literal: I hope an edict will order the Ministry of Justice to classify all capital cases decided throughout the realm and report them annually to the court, to assist observation and reflection."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an edict order the Ministry of Justice to classify all capital cases decided throughout the realm and report them annually to the court, to assist observation and reflection."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 凡在京班直諸軍請糧，斗斛不足，出戍之家尤甚。

translations.literal: For all garrison troops on duty rotation in the capital requesting grain rations, the measures were insufficient, especially for families of men deployed on frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: For all garrison troops on duty rotation in the capital requesting grain rations, the measures were insufficient, especially for families of men deployed on frontier duty.

sentences.zh: 倉吏自以在官無祿，恣為侵漁。

translations.literal: Granary clerks, considering themselves unsalaried while in office, freely engaged in extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Granary clerks, considering themselves unsalaried while in office, freely engaged in extortion.

sentences.zh: 神宗謂非所以愛養將士之意，於是詔三司，始立諸倉丐取法。

translations.literal: Shenzong said this was not the way to cherish and sustain officers and soldiers; thereupon he ordered the Three Departments to establish for the first time the Granary Extortion Law.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said this was not the way to cherish and sustain officers and soldiers; thereupon he ordered the Three Departments to establish for the first time the Granary Extortion Law.

sentences.zh: 而中書請主典役人，歲增祿至一萬八千九百餘緡。

translations.literal: The Secretariat requested salaries for chief clerks and laborers, increasing annual pay to more than eighteen thousand nine hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat requested salaries for chief clerks and laborers, increasing annual pay to more than eighteen thousand nine hundred strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 凡丐取不滿百錢，徒一年，每百錢則加一等；

translations.literal: For all extortion of less than one hundred cash, penal servitude for one year; for each additional hundred cash one degree was added;
translations.idiomatic: For all extortion of less than one hundred cash, penal servitude for one year; for each additional hundred cash one degree was added;

sentences.zh: 千錢流二千里，每千錢則加一等，罪止流三千里。

translations.literal: one thousand cash, exile two thousand li; for each additional thousand cash one degree was added, the punishment stopping at exile three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: one thousand cash, exile two thousand li; for each additional thousand cash one degree was added, the punishment stopping at exile three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其行貨及過致者，減首罪二等。

translations.literal: Those who gave bribes and those who transmitted them had their punishment reduced two degrees below the principal offense.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gave bribes and those who transmitted them had their punishment reduced two degrees below the principal offense.

sentences.zh: 徒者皆配五百里，其賞百千；

translations.literal: Those sentenced to penal servitude were all assigned five hundred li away, with a reward of one hundred strings;
translations.idiomatic: Those sentenced to penal servitude were all assigned five hundred li away, with a reward of one hundred strings;

sentences.zh: 流者皆配千里，賞二百千；

translations.literal: those sentenced to exile were all assigned a thousand li away, with a reward of two hundred strings;
translations.idiomatic: those sentenced to exile were all assigned a thousand li away, with a reward of two hundred strings;

sentences.zh: 滿十千，為首者配沙門島，賞三百千，自首則除其罪。

translations.literal: at ten thousand cash, the ringleader was assigned to Shamen Island, with a reward of three hundred strings; self-confession removed the crime.
translations.idiomatic: at ten thousand cash, the ringleader was assigned to Shamen Island, with a reward of three hundred strings; self-confession removed the crime.

sentences.zh: 凡更定約束十條行之。

translations.literal: In all, ten revised regulations were established and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In all, ten revised regulations were established and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 其後內則政府，外則監司，多倣此法。

translations.literal: Thereafter, within the government and among circuit supervisors without, many modeled themselves on this law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, within the government and among circuit supervisors without, many modeled themselves on this law.

sentences.zh: 內外歲增吏祿至百餘萬緡，皆取諸坊場，河渡，市利，免行、役剩息錢。

translations.literal: Within and without, annual increases in clerical salaries reached more than a million strings, all drawn from market stalls, river crossings, market profits, exemption fees, service surpluses, and interest monies.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without, annual increases in clerical salaries reached more than a million strings, all drawn from market stalls, river crossings, market profits, exemption fees, service surpluses, and interest monies.

sentences.zh: 久之，議臣欲稍緩倉法，編敕所修立告捕獲倉法給賞條，自一百千分等至三百千，而按問者減半給之。

translations.literal: After some time, deliberating officials wished slightly to relax the granary law; the Statute Compilation Office revised the reward provisions for reporting and capturing granary-law offenders, ranging by degree from one hundred to three hundred strings, while interrogators received half.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, deliberating officials wished slightly to relax the granary law; the Statute Compilation Office revised the reward provisions for reporting and capturing granary-law offenders, ranging by degree from one hundred to three hundred strings, while interrogators received half.

sentences.zh: 中書請依所定，詔仍舊給全賞，雖按問，亦全給。

translations.literal: The Secretariat requested following what was fixed; an edict ordered that full rewards still be given as before, and even interrogators received the full amount.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat requested following what was fixed; an edict ordered that full rewards still be given as before, and even interrogators received the full amount.

sentences.zh: 呂嘉問嘗請，行貨者宜止以不應為坐之，刑部始減其罪。

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen once requested that those who gave bribes should be punished only under the statute for improper conduct; the Ministry of Justice then reduced their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen once requested that those who gave bribes should be punished only under the statute for improper conduct; the Ministry of Justice then reduced their punishment.

sentences.zh: 及哲宗初，嘗罷重祿法，而紹聖復仍舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhezong's reign, the heavy-salary law was once abolished, but under Shaosheng the old practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhezong's reign, the heavy-salary law was once abolished, but under Shaosheng the old practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，立盜賊重法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, the Heavy Law on Bandits and Thieves was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xining, the Heavy Law on Bandits and Thieves was established.

sentences.zh: 凡盜罪當死者，籍其家貲以賞告人，妻子編置千里；

translations.literal: For all theft crimes meriting death, household property was registered to reward informants, and wives and children were registered and resettled a thousand li away;
translations.idiomatic: For all theft crimes meriting death, household property was registered to reward informants, and wives and children were registered and resettled a thousand li away;

sentences.zh: 遇赦若災傷減等者，配遠惡地。

translations.literal: if amnesty or disaster relief reduced the sentence, they were assigned to distant and harsh lands.
translations.idiomatic: if amnesty or disaster relief reduced the sentence, they were assigned to distant and harsh lands.

sentences.zh: 罪當徙、流者，配嶺表；

translations.literal: Those whose crimes merited penal servitude or exile were assigned beyond the mountain passes;
translations.idiomatic: Those whose crimes merited penal servitude or exile were assigned beyond the mountain passes;

sentences.zh: 流罪會降者，配三千里，籍其家貲之半為賞，妻子遞降等有差。

translations.literal: exile sentences meeting reduction were assigned three thousand li away, half the household property was registered as reward, and wives and children were reduced by successive degrees with differences.
translations.idiomatic: exile sentences meeting reduction were assigned three thousand li away, half the household property was registered as reward, and wives and children were reduced by successive degrees accordingly.

sentences.zh: 應編配者，雖會赦，不移不釋。

translations.literal: Those subject to registered assignment, even if meeting amnesty, were neither transferred nor released.
translations.idiomatic: Those subject to registered assignment, even if meeting amnesty, were neither transferred nor released.

sentences.zh: 凡囊橐之家，劫盜死罪，情重者斬，餘皆配遠惡地，籍其家貲之半為賞。

translations.literal: For all households that harbored bandits, robbery meriting death: if the circumstances were severe, decapitation; the rest were all assigned to distant and harsh lands, and half the household property was registered as reward.
translations.idiomatic: For all households that harbored bandits, robbery meriting death: if the circumstances were severe, decapitation; the rest were all assigned to distant and harsh lands, and half the household property was registered as reward.

sentences.zh: 盜罪當徒、流者，配五百里，籍其家貲三之一為賞。

translations.literal: Theft crimes meriting penal servitude or exile were assigned five hundred li away, and one-third of household property was registered as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Theft crimes meriting penal servitude or exile were assigned five hundred li away, and one-third of household property was registered as reward.

sentences.zh: 竊盜三犯，杖配五百里或州。

translations.literal: Petty theft on the third offense, after beating, was assigned five hundred li away or to a neighboring prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Petty theft on the third offense, after beating, was assigned five hundred li away or to a neighboring prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雖非重法之地，而囊橐重法之人，以重法論。

translations.literal: Even if not in a heavy-law region, those who harbored offenders under the heavy law were judged by the heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: Even if not in a heavy-law region, those who harbored offenders subject to the heavy law were judged by the heavy law.

sentences.zh: 其知縣、捕盜官皆用舉者，或武臣為尉。

translations.literal: Their district magistrates and bandit-capture officials were all men recommended for appointment, or military officers serving as captains.
translations.idiomatic: Their district magistrates and bandit-capture officials were all men recommended for appointment, or military officers serving as captains.

sentences.zh: 盜發十人以上，限內捕半不獲，劾罪取旨。

translations.literal: When banditry involved ten or more persons, if half were not captured within the deadline, guilt was investigated and imperial decision sought.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry involved ten or more persons, if half were not captured within the deadline, guilt was investigated and imperial decision sought.

sentences.zh: 若復殺官吏，及累殺三人，焚舍屋百間，或?行州縣之內，劫掠江海船之中，非重地，亦以重論。

translations.literal: If they further killed officials, or cumulatively killed three persons, burned a hundred dwellings, or acted in groups within prefectures and counties and plundered within river and sea boats and rafts—even if not in a heavy-law region, they were also judged by the heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: If they further killed officials, or cumulatively killed three persons, burned a hundred dwellings, or acted in groups within prefectures and counties and plundered river and sea boats and rafts—even if not in a heavy-law region, they were also judged by the heavy law.

sentences.zh: 凡重法地，嘉祐中，始於開封府諸縣，後稍及諸州。

translations.literal: For all heavy-law regions, in the Jiayou era it began in the counties of Kaifeng Prefecture, and later gradually extended to various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For all heavy-law regions, in the Jiayou era it began in the counties of Kaifeng Prefecture, and later gradually extended to various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以開封府東明、考城、長垣縣，京西滑州，淮南宿州，河北澶州，京東應天府、濮、齊、徐、濟、單、兗、鄆、沂州、淮陽軍，亦立重法，著為令。

translations.literal: Dongming, Kaocheng, and Changyuan counties of Kaifeng Prefecture, Huazhou in Jingxi, Suzhou in Huainan, Danzhou in Hebei, Yingtian Prefecture in Jingdong, and the prefectures of Pu, Qi, Xu, Ji, Shan, Yan, Yun, and Yi, plus Huaiyang Commandery, also established the heavy law, which was written as ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming, Kaocheng, and Changyuan counties of Kaifeng Prefecture, Huazhou in Jingxi, Suzhou in Huainan, Danzhou in Hebei, Yingtian Prefecture in Jingdong, and the prefectures of Pu, Qi, Xu, Ji, Shan, Yan, Yun, and Yi, plus Huaiyang Commandery, also established the heavy law, which was written as ordinance.

sentences.zh: 至元豐時，河北、京東、淮南、福建等路皆用重法，郡縣寖益廣矣。

translations.literal: By the Yuanfeng era, the circuits of Hebei, Jingdong, Huainan, Fujian, and others all applied the heavy law, and prefectures and counties grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanfeng era, the circuits of Hebei, Jingdong, Huainan, Fujian, and others all applied the heavy law, and its reach among prefectures and counties grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 元豐敕，重法地分，劫盜五人以上，凶惡者，方論以重法。

translations.literal: The Yuanfeng edict stated that in heavy-law regions, robbery by five or more persons, if vicious and wicked, might then be judged by the heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng edict stated that in heavy-law regions, only robbery by five or more vicious and wicked persons might be judged by the heavy law.

sentences.zh: 紹聖後，有犯即坐，不計人數。

translations.literal: After Shaosheng, any offense immediately incurred punishment, without counting the number of persons.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaosheng, any offense immediately incurred punishment, without regard to the number of persons involved.

sentences.zh: 復立妻孥編管法。

translations.literal: The Law on Registered Control of Wives and Children was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: The Law on Registered Control of Wives and Children was reestablished.

sentences.zh: 至元符三年，因刑部有請，詔改依舊敕。

translations.literal: By the third year of Yuanfu, because the Ministry of Justice submitted a request, an edict ordered reversion to the old edict.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of Yuanfu, because the Ministry of Justice submitted a request, an edict ordered reversion to the old edict.

sentences.zh: 先是，曾布建言：「盜情有重輕，贓有多少。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zeng Bu submitted a proposal: "The circumstances of theft have degrees of severity, and stolen goods vary in amount.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zeng Bu submitted a proposal: "The circumstances of theft have degrees of severity, and stolen goods vary in amount.

sentences.zh: 今以贓論罪，則劫貧家情雖重，而以贓少減免，劫富室情雖輕，而以贓重論死。

translations.literal: Now judging guilt by stolen goods, robbing a poor household though the circumstances are severe is mitigated because the goods are few, while robbing a rich household though the circumstances are mild is judged death because the goods are great.
translations.idiomatic: Now judging guilt by stolen goods, robbing a poor household though the circumstances are severe is mitigated because the goods are few, while robbing a rich household though the circumstances are mild is judged death because the goods are great.

sentences.zh: 是盜之生死，係於主之貧富也。

translations.literal: Thus whether a thief lives or dies depends on the victim's wealth or poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether a thief lives or dies depends on the victim's wealth or poverty.

sentences.zh: 至於傷人，情狀亦殊。

translations.literal: As for injuring persons, the circumstances also differ.
translations.idiomatic: As for injuring persons, the circumstances also differ.

sentences.zh: 以手足毆人，偶傷肌體，與夫兵刃湯火，固有間矣，而均謂之傷。

translations.literal: Striking a person with hands or feet and accidentally injuring the flesh is certainly distinct from weapons, boiling water, or fire, yet all are equally called injury.
translations.idiomatic: Striking a person with hands or feet and accidentally injuring the flesh is certainly distinct from weapons, boiling water, or fire, yet all are equally called injury.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖許奏裁，而州郡或奏或否，死生之分，特幸與不幸爾。

translations.literal: Although the court permitted memorials for imperial decision, prefectures and commanderies sometimes memorialized and sometimes did not—the difference between life and death was merely luck and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court permitted memorials for imperial decision, prefectures and commanderies sometimes memorialized and sometimes did not—the difference between life and death was merely luck and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 不若一變舊法，凡以贓定罪及傷人情狀不至切害者，皆從罪止之法。

translations.literal: Better to change the old law at once: for all cases judged by stolen goods and injuries whose circumstances do not reach grave harm, all should follow the law limiting punishment to the minimum.
translations.idiomatic: Better to change the old law at once: for all cases judged by stolen goods and injuries whose circumstances do not reach grave harm, all should follow the law limiting punishment to the minimum.

sentences.zh: 其用兵刃湯火，情狀酷毒，乃汙辱良家，或入州縣鎮砦行劫，若驅虜官吏巡防人等，不以傷與不傷，凡情不可貸者，皆處以死刑 ，則輕重不失其當矣。」

translations.literal: Those who use weapons, boiling water, or fire with cruel and poisonous circumstances, who defile respectable households, or enter prefectures, counties, towns, and stockades to rob, or who drive off and capture officials and patrol guards—regardless of injury or no injury—for all whose circumstances cannot be pardoned, all should receive the death penalty; then severity and leniency would not miss their proper measure."
translations.idiomatic: Those who use weapons, boiling water, or fire with cruel and poisonous circumstances, who defile respectable households, or enter prefectures, counties, towns, and stockades to rob, or who drive off and capture officials and patrol guards—regardless of whether injury occurred—for all whose circumstances cannot be pardoned, all should receive the death penalty; then severity and leniency would not miss their proper measure."

sentences.zh: 及布為相，始從其議，詔有司改法。

translations.literal: When Bu became chief councilor, his proposal was at last adopted, and an edict ordered officials to revise the law.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu became chief councilor, his proposal was at last adopted, and an edict ordered officials to revise the law.

sentences.zh: 未幾，侍御史陳次升言：「祖宗仁政，加於天下者甚廣。

translations.literal: Before long, Attendant Censor Chen Cisheng said: "The benevolent policies of the imperial ancestors extended very broadly over the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Attendant Censor Chen Cisheng said: "The benevolent policies of the imperial ancestors extended very broadly over the realm.

sentences.zh: 刑法之重，改而從輕者至多。

translations.literal: Among heavy punishments in the penal code, those revised toward leniency were extremely many.
translations.idiomatic: Among heavy punishments in the penal code, those revised toward leniency were extremely many.

sentences.zh: 惟是強盜之法，特加重者，蓋以禁姦宄而惠良民也。

translations.literal: Only the law on robbery was specially made heavier, intending to restrain treachery and wickedness and benefit good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Only the law on robbery was specially made heavier, intending to restrain treachery and wickedness and benefit good commoners.

sentences.zh: 近朝廷改法，詔以強盜計贓應絞者，並增一倍；

translations.literal: Recently the court revised the law, ordering that for robbery judged by stolen goods meriting strangulation, the amount was doubled;
translations.idiomatic: Recently the court revised the law, ordering that for robbery judged by stolen goods meriting strangulation, the threshold was doubled;

sentences.zh: 贓滿不傷人，及雖傷人而情輕者奏裁。

translations.literal: when stolen goods reached the threshold without injury, or though injury occurred the circumstances were mild, memorials for imperial decision were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: when stolen goods reached the threshold without injury, or though injury occurred the circumstances were mild, memorials for imperial decision were submitted.

sentences.zh: 法行之後，民受其弊。

translations.literal: After the law was implemented, the people suffered its harm.
translations.idiomatic: After the law was implemented, the people suffered its harm.

sentences.zh: 被害之家，以盜無必死之理，不敢告官，而鄰里亦不為之擒捕，恐怨仇報復。

translations.literal: Victim households, believing bandits had no certainty of death, dared not report to officials, and neighbors also would not capture them for fear of vengeful reprisal.
translations.idiomatic: Victim households, believing bandits had no certainty of death, dared not report to officials, and neighbors also would not capture them for fear of vengeful reprisal.

sentences.zh: 故賊益逞，重法地分尤甚。

translations.literal: Thus bandits grew ever bolder, especially in heavy-law regions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus bandits grew ever bolder, especially in heavy-law regions.

sentences.zh: 恐養成大寇，以貽國家之患，請復行舊法。」

translations.literal: I fear this will nurture great bandits and bequeath trouble to the state; I request restoring the old law."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this will nurture great bandit gangs and leave trouble for the state; I ask that the old law be restored."

sentences.zh: 布罷相，翰林學士徐勣復言其不便，乃詔如舊法，前詔勿行。

translations.literal: When Bu left the chancellorship, Hanlin Academician Xu Ji again spoke of its inconvenience, and an edict restored the old law; the previous edict was not to be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu left the chancellorship, Hanlin Academician Xu Ji again argued that the change was unworkable, and an edict ordered a return to the old law; the earlier edict was revoked.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸路經略、鈐轄，不得便宜斬配百姓。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier commissioners and jurisdictional commissioners on all circuits were not permitted to execute or exile commoners at their discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, frontier commissioners and jurisdictional commissioners in every circuit were forbidden to execute or banish commoners on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 趙抃嘗知成都，乃言當獨許成都四路。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian, who had once served as prefect of Chengdu, then argued that this alone should be permitted for the Four Circuits of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian, who had once governed Chengdu, argued that discretionary power should be granted only to the four Chengdu circuits.

sentences.zh: 王安石執不可，而中書、樞密院同立法許之。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi insisted this was impermissible, but the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs jointly legislated to allow it.
