translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi held that this was impermissible, yet the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs jointly enacted a law permitting it.

sentences.zh: 其後，謝景初奏：「成都妄以便宜誅釋，多不當。」

translations.literal: Subsequently, Xie Jingchu memorialized: "Chengdu has wantonly exercised discretionary power to execute or release, mostly inappropriately."
translations.idiomatic: Later Xie Jingchu memorialized: "Chengdu has wantonly exercised discretionary power to execute or release offenders, mostly without justification."

sentences.zh: 於是中書復刪定敕文，惟軍士犯罪及邊防機速，許特斷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat again revised the edict text: only when soldiers committed crimes or frontier emergencies were urgent was special adjudication permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Secretariat again revised the edict text so that special summary judgment was permitted only for crimes by soldiers and urgent frontier emergencies.

sentences.zh: 及抃移成都，又請立法，御史劉孝孫亦為之請依舊便宜從事，安石寢其奏。

translations.literal: When Bian was transferred to Chengdu, he again requested legislation; Censor Liu Xiaosun also petitioned on his behalf to resume discretionary action as before; Anshi shelved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian was transferred to Chengdu, he again requested legislation, and Censor Liu Xiaosun also petitioned that he be allowed to act at discretion as before; Anshi shelved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 武臣犯贓，經赦敘復後，更立年考升遷。

translations.literal: When military officers committed corruption, after amnesty and restoration they again established annual review for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers who committed corruption, once restored after amnesty, were again subject to annual review and promotion.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若此，何以戒貪吏？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If this is so, how are greedy officials to be warned?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "If that is allowed, how will greedy officials be deterred?"

sentences.zh: 故命改法。

translations.literal: Therefore he ordered the law changed.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered the law revised.

sentences.zh: 熙寧六年，樞密都承旨曾孝寬等定議上之，大概倣文臣敘法而少增損爾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining, Bureau Director Zeng Xiaokuan and others fixed the regulations and submitted them—generally following the civil-officer restoration law with slight additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xining, Bureau Director Zeng Xiaokuan and others drafted regulations and submitted them, largely following the civil-officer restoration law with minor adjustments.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：「品官犯罪，按察之官並奏劾聽旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict: "When ranked officials commit crimes, investigating officials shall all memorialize impeachment and await imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict ordered: "When ranked officials commit crimes, investigating officials must memorialize impeachment and await imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 毋得擅捕繫、罷其職奉。」

translations.literal: They may not on their own arrest, detain, or suspend salary and emoluments."
translations.idiomatic: They may not on their own authority arrest, detain, or suspend salary and emoluments."

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，成都府、利路鈐轄言：「往時川峽絹匹為錢二千六百，以此估贓，兩鐵錢得比銅錢之一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Chengdu Prefecture and Lizhou jurisdictional commissioner reported: "Formerly a bolt of silk in the Chuanxia region was valued at 2,600 cash; by this valuation of stolen goods, two iron coins equaled one copper coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Chengdu Prefecture and Lizhou jurisdictional commissioner reported: "Formerly a bolt of silk in the Sichuan gorges was worth 2,600 cash; stolen goods were valued accordingly, so that two iron coins counted as one copper coin.

sentences.zh: 近絹匹不過千三百，估贓二匹乃得一匹之罪，多不至重法。」

translations.literal: Recently a bolt of silk is no more than 1,300; valuing stolen goods, two bolts only merit punishment for one bolt, mostly not reaching the heavy law."
translations.idiomatic: Now a bolt of silk is worth no more than 1,300; under current valuation two bolts of stolen silk only incur the penalty for one, so offenders often escape the heavy law."

sentences.zh: 令法寺定以一錢半當銅錢之一。

translations.literal: The Office of the Review of Laws was ordered to fix one and a half iron coins as equal to one copper coin.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Review of Laws was ordered to fix the rate at one and a half iron coins to one copper coin.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年， 刑部、大理寺定制：「凡斷讞奏獄，每二十緡以上為大事，十緡以上為中事，不滿十緡為小事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, the Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review fixed regulations: "For all submitted cases after judgment, twenty strings of cash and above constitutes a major matter, ten strings and above a medium matter, less than ten strings a minor matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanyou, the Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review established rules: "For all cases submitted after judgment, twenty strings of cash or more counted as a major matter, ten strings or more as a medium matter, and less than ten strings as a minor matter.

sentences.zh: 大事以十二日，中事九日，小事四日為限。

translations.literal: Major matters have a limit of twelve days, medium matters nine days, minor matters four days.
translations.idiomatic: Major matters were limited to twelve days, medium matters to nine days, and minor matters to four days.

sentences.zh: 若在京、八路大事十日，中事五日，小事三日。

translations.literal: In the capital and Eight Circuits, major matters ten days, medium matters five days, minor matters three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital and the Eight Circuits, the limits were ten days for major matters, five for medium matters, and three for minor matters.

sentences.zh: 臺察及刑部舉劾約法狀並十日，三省、樞密院再送各減半。

translations.literal: Censorial offices and the Ministry of Justice submitting summary impeachment memorials all ten days; when resubmitted by the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs, each is halved.
translations.idiomatic: Cases from censorial offices and Ministry of Justice summary impeachments were allotted ten days; when resubmitted by the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs, each limit was halved.

sentences.zh: 有故量展，不得過五日。

translations.literal: When cause exists to extend appropriately, it may not exceed five days.
translations.idiomatic: Extensions for good cause were permitted, but could not exceed five days.

sentences.zh: 凡公案日限，大事以三十五日，中事二十五日，小事十日為限。

translations.literal: For all public case time limits, major matters thirty-five days, medium matters twenty-five days, minor matters ten days as limit.
translations.idiomatic: For all ordinary case deadlines, major matters were limited to thirty-five days, medium matters to twenty-five days, and minor matters to ten days.

sentences.zh: 在京、八路大事以三十日，中事半之，小事三之一。

translations.literal: In the capital and Eight Circuits, major matters thirty days, medium matters half that, minor matters one-third.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital and the Eight Circuits, major matters were limited to thirty days, medium matters to half that, and minor matters to one-third.

sentences.zh: 臺察及 刑部並三十日。

translations.literal: Censorial offices and the Ministry of Justice all thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Cases from censorial offices and the Ministry of Justice were allotted thirty days.

sentences.zh: 每十日，斷用七日，議用三日。」

translations.literal: Of every ten days, seven for adjudication, three for deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Of every ten days, seven were for adjudication and three for deliberation."

sentences.zh: 五年，詔命官犯罪，事干邊防軍政，文臣申尚書省，武臣申樞密院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict: when ranked officials commit crimes involving frontier defense and military affairs, civil officials report to the Ministry of Personnel, military officials to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, an edict ordered that when ranked officials committed crimes touching frontier defense and military affairs, civil officials were to report to the Ministry of Personnel and military officials to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 中丞蘇轍言：「舊制，文臣、吏民斷罪公案歸中書，武臣、軍士歸樞密，而斷例輕重，悉不相知。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Su Che said: "Under the old system, civil officials and commoners' criminal cases went to the Secretariat; military officers and soldiers to the Bureau of Military Affairs—yet precedents for severity were entirely unknown to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Su Che said: "Under the old system, criminal cases involving civil officials and commoners went to the Secretariat, while those involving military officers and soldiers went to the Bureau of Military Affairs, yet neither side knew the other's sentencing precedents.

sentences.zh: 元豐更定官制，斷獄公案並由大理、刑部申尚書省，然後上中書省取旨。

translations.literal: When Yuanfeng reorganized offices, criminal cases all went through the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice to the Ministry of Personnel, then up to the Secretariat for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reforms reorganized the bureaucracy, all criminal cases passed through the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice to the Ministry of Personnel, and then up to the Secretariat for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 自是斷獄輕重比例，始得歸一，天下稱明焉。

translations.literal: From then on the scale of severity in adjudication could be unified, and the realm praised its clarity.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the scale of severity in sentencing could be unified, and the realm praised the clarity of the system.

sentences.zh: 今復分隸樞密，必有罪同斷異，失元豐本意，請並歸三省。

translations.literal: Now reverting to separate assignment under the Bureau of Military Affairs, there will inevitably be identical crimes with differing judgments, losing the original intent of Yuanfeng—I request all be returned to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Now that cases are again divided under the Bureau of Military Affairs, identical crimes will inevitably receive different judgments, betraying the original intent of the Yuanfeng reforms; I ask that all cases be returned to the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 其事干邊防軍政者，令樞密院同進取旨，則事體歸一，而兵政大臣各得其職。」

translations.literal: When matters involve frontier defense and military affairs, let the Bureau of Military Affairs jointly submit for imperial decision—then the substance of affairs will be unified, and military affairs ministers each fulfill their duties."
translations.idiomatic: When a case touches frontier defense and military affairs, let the Bureau of Military Affairs jointly submit it for imperial decision; then the substance of affairs will be unified, and the ministers of military affairs will each fulfill their proper duties."

sentences.zh: 六年，乃詔：「文武官有犯同按干邊防軍政者，刑部定斷，仍三省、樞密院同取旨。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict: "When civil and military officials commit crimes jointly investigated involving frontier defense and military affairs, the Ministry of Justice shall fix judgment, and the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs shall jointly obtain imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict ordered: "When civil and military officials commit crimes jointly investigated in matters touching frontier defense and military affairs, the Ministry of Justice shall determine judgment, and the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs shall jointly obtain imperial decision."

sentences.zh: 刑部論：「佃客犯主，加凡人一等。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice statute: "When tenant farmers offend their master, one grade above ordinary persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice ruled: "When tenant farmers offend their masters, the penalty is one grade above that for ordinary persons.

sentences.zh: 主犯之，杖以下勿論，徒以上減凡人一等。

translations.literal: When the master offends them, beating punishments and below are not prosecuted; penal servitude and above are reduced one grade from ordinary persons.
translations.idiomatic: When the master offends them, beatings and lesser punishments are not prosecuted; penal servitude and above are reduced one grade below that for ordinary persons.

sentences.zh: 謀殺盜詐，有所規求避免而犯者，不減。

translations.literal: Premeditated murder, robbery, or fraud, or offenses committed with some design to gain or avoid something—no reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Premeditated murder, robbery, or fraud, or offenses committed with some design to gain advantage or evade obligation, receive no reduction.

sentences.zh: 因毆致死者不刺面，配鄰州，情重者奏裁。

translations.literal: If beating causes death, no tattooing of the face; exile to a neighboring prefecture; where circumstances are severe, submit for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: If beating causes death, the offender is not tattooed but is exiled to a neighboring prefecture; where circumstances are grave, the case is submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 凡命士死於官或去位，其送徒道亡，則部轄將校、節級與首率眾者徒一年，情輕則杖百，雖自首不免。」

translations.literal: For all appointees who die in office or after leaving post, if convicts escape en route during escort, the unit commander, squad leader, and chief ringleader receive one year penal servitude; if circumstances are mild, one hundred blows; even self-surrender does not exempt."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an appointee dies in office or after leaving his post, if convicts escape en route during escort, the unit commander, squad leader, and chief ringleader receive one year of penal servitude; if circumstances are mild, one hundred blows; even voluntary surrender does not exempt them."

sentences.zh: 政和間，詔：「品官犯罪，三問不承，即奏請追攝；

translations.literal: During Zhenghe, an edict: "When ranked officials commit crimes, if after three interrogations they do not confess, immediately memorialize requesting summons;
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era, an edict ordered: "When ranked officials commit crimes, if after three interrogations they do not confess, officials shall immediately memorialize requesting their summons;

sentences.zh: 若情理重害而拒隱，方許枷訊。

translations.literal: Only if circumstances are gravely harmful and they refuse concealment is shackled interrogation permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shackled interrogation is permitted only when the circumstances are gravely harmful and the offender refuses to disclose them.

sentences.zh: 邇來有司廢法，不原輕重，枷訊與常人無異，將使人有輕吾爵祿之心。

translations.literal: Recently officials have abandoned the law, disregarding severity and leniency, applying shackled interrogation no differently from common persons—this will make people look lightly upon our ranks and stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Recently officials have abandoned the law, disregarding degrees of severity, and apply shackled interrogation no differently than to commoners—this will lead people to hold our ranks and stipends in contempt.

sentences.zh: 可申明條令，以稱欽恤之意。」

translations.literal: The regulations should be clarified to accord with the intent of imperial compassion."
translations.idiomatic: The regulations should be clarified to reflect the emperor's compassionate intent."

sentences.zh: 又詔；

translations.literal: Another edict was issued:
translations.idiomatic: Another edict followed:

sentences.zh: 「宗子犯罪，庭訓示辱。

translations.literal: "When imperial clansmen commit crimes, court discipline serves as humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: "When imperial clansmen commit crimes, household admonishment at court suffices as humiliation.

sentences.zh: 比有去衣受杖，傷膚敗體，有惻朕懷。

translations.literal: Recently some have stripped for beating, wounding flesh and harming the body—this moves Our heart to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Recently some have been stripped for beating, wounding flesh and marring the body—this moves Us to compassion.

sentences.zh: 其令大宗正司恪守條制，違者以違御筆論。」

translations.literal: Let the Directorate of the Imperial Clan strictly observe the regulations; violators shall be judged as disobeying the emperor's personal order."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Directorate of the Imperial Clan strictly observe the regulations; violators shall be punished as defying the emperor's personal command."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「其情理重害，別被處分。

translations.literal: It was also said: "Where circumstances are gravely harmful, separate punishment shall be applied.
translations.idiomatic: It was also ordered: "Where circumstances are gravely harmful, separate punishment shall be applied.

sentences.zh: 若罪至徒、流，方許制勘，餘止以眾證為定，仍取伏辨，無得輒加捶考。

translations.literal: Only when guilt reaches penal servitude or exile is formal inquest permitted; otherwise conviction rests on collective testimony alone, with written confession obtained—beating and torture must not be casually applied.
translations.idiomatic: Formal inquest is permitted only when guilt reaches penal servitude or exile; otherwise conviction rests on collective testimony alone, with written confession obtained—beating and torture must not be applied casually.

sentences.zh: 其合庭訓者，並送大宗正司，以副朕敦睦九族之意。」

translations.literal: Those fit for court discipline shall all be sent to the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, to fulfill Our intent of nurturing harmony among the nine kinship ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Those fit for household admonishment shall all be sent to the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, in keeping with Our intent to nurture harmony among the nine kinship ranks."

sentences.zh: 中書省言：「律，『在官犯罪，去官勿論』。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "The code states, 'When one in office commits a crime, upon leaving office it is not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat said: "The code provides, 'Crimes committed while in office are not prosecuted once the offender has left office.

sentences.zh: 蓋為命官立文。

translations.literal: This was establishing text for appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: That provision was written for appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 其後相因，掌典去官，亦用去官免罪，有犯則解役歸農，幸免重罪。」

translations.literal: Subsequently by succession, when clerks in charge left office they also used leaving office to escape guilt; when they offended they were released from service and returned to farming, narrowly escaping serious punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently the practice spread by precedent: when clerks in charge left office they too invoked leaving office to escape punishment; offenders were released from service and sent back to farming, narrowly avoiding serious penalties."

sentences.zh: 詔改政和敕掌典解役從去官法。

translations.literal: An edict amended the Zhenghe edict: clerks released from service follow the leaving-office law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict amended the Zhenghe edict so that clerks released from service and returned to farming were governed by the leaving-office law.

sentences.zh: 左道亂法，妖言惑眾，先王之所不赦，至宋尤重其禁。

translations.literal: Heterodox ways that disorder the law and demonic speech that deludes the masses—what the ancient kings did not pardon—the Song especially strengthened its prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox cults that subvert the law and sorcerous talk that misleads the masses were what the ancient kings never pardoned; under the Song the prohibitions were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 凡傳習妖教，夜聚曉散，與夫殺人祭祀之類，皆著于法，訶察甚嚴。

translations.literal: All who transmitted and practiced demonic teachings, gathering at night and dispersing at dawn, and such matters as killing persons for sacrifice—all were set forth in law, with scrutiny and investigation extremely strict.
translations.idiomatic: All who transmitted heterodox teachings, gathering at night and dispersing at dawn, as well as such practices as human sacrifice, were codified in law and subjected to rigorous investigation.

sentences.zh: 故姦軌不逞之民，無以動搖愚俗。

translations.literal: Thus wicked and lawless persons had no means to sway the foolish masses.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wicked and lawless persons had no means to sway the credulous populace.

sentences.zh: 間有為之，隨輒報敗，其事不足紀也。

translations.literal: Occasionally some did so, but were immediately exposed and ruined; such matters are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally some tried, but were promptly exposed and crushed; such incidents scarcely merit mention.
